boundary: This ledger records LINKAGE, not coverage. A status says which shipped mechanical controls cite a rule, and each control carries a residue naming what it does not catch; the residue is the honest half of every claim. None of the statuses means a rule is enforced: gate-linked means at least one deterministic repository gate cites the rule, hook-linked means at least one runtime hook cites it and no gate does, prose-only means no shipped control cites it and the rule binds through the governing prose alone. Nothing in this file is a completeness or coverage measure, and deriving a score from it misreads it.

hooks.residue: Covers the required-absolute file_path of Read, Write, and Edit and the required-absolute notebook_path of NotebookEdit (absolute by each tool's own contract, so the relative-to-a-named-root carve-out never applies to them), plus the OPTIONAL path search root of Glob and Grep (which should be absolute), and the MultiEdit file_path kept for LEGACY COMPATIBILITY. Each field name is bound to a Claude Code tool schema (Read/Write/Edit -> file_path, NotebookEdit -> notebook_path, Glob/Grep -> optional path); MultiEdit -> file_path is retained as a legacy-compatibility wire (MultiEdit is NOT in the current Claude Code built-in tool index, so its mapping is kept only so an adopter on an older or re-enabled MultiEdit is still covered, never an assertion that MultiEdit is a current tool). This STRUCTURED coverage binds ONLY those enumerated tool schemas: a path carried in any OTHER tool field, tool, or parameter, or in Bash command text, is out of scope here (the sibling abs-paths-bash floor covers only a cd/pushd destination and a redirect target in Bash, nothing else). Absoluteness is judged by the runtime's own path semantics (PurePosixPath/PureWindowsPath.is_absolute), so a drive-RELATIVE 'C:file', a bare 'C:', and a rooted-but-driveless leading-backslash path are correctly NOT absolute, while a POSIX '/x', a drive-absolute 'C:\x'/'C:/x', and a UNC '\\server\share' are; a '~'-prefixed path is not expanded and is not absolute. Honours the carve-out: the relative search PATTERN of Glob and Grep is legitimately relative to its named root and is never judged, and a rootless call (no path) names the current directory as that root and is allowed. Fails CLOSED: a tool_input that is not a readable mapping, or a required file_path/notebook_path that is absent or not a non-empty string, denies rather than passing (closing the earlier fail-open where a malformed tool_input collapsed to an empty mapping and took the search-root allow branch). Does NOT judge whether an absolute path points at the INTENDED target (absoluteness is not intent), and is platform=claude-code only.

A SEPARATE best-effort Bash layer of abspth, distinct from the structured typed-path guard (abs-paths), whose structured coverage binds only the enumerated tool schemas and never Bash command text. This is a CONSERVATIVE FLOOR, ASK-defaulting and NEVER denying (the human confirming is the opt-out): it judges ONLY two positions that silently resolve against the current working directory, a cd/pushd DESTINATION operand and a redirection TARGET, and NEVER an arbitrary command operand (a relative path argument to any other command is deliberately NOT judged, to avoid over-firing). A relative or unresolvable such position ASKS; an absolute one, an UNQUOTED CURRENT-USER tilde destination ('~' or '~/x', which the shell expands to $HOME so it is cwd-independent), a bare 'cd'/'pushd' and the OLDPWD 'cd -' (both only absent ANY leading inline env-assignment, see below), the real cd/pushd option flags (cd -L/-P/-e/-@, pushd -n, singly or bundled), a pushd stack rotation (+N/-N), and a numeric/'-' descriptor duplication (2>&1) allow. The tilde-ALLOW is NARROWED to the current-user forms and gated on a WHOLE-TILDE-PREFIX-UNQUOTED signal, NOT on the broader token-wide opacity flag: it is True only when the token begins with an unquoted '~' AND the ENTIRE tilde-prefix (from that '~' up to the first UNQUOTED '/', or end of word) is unquoted and unescaped, which is exactly when bash performs tilde-expansion. So a QUOTED leading tilde, EVEN with an unquoted expansion/glob/brace TAIL (the "~"/x*, '~'/x?, "~"/$V, "~/repo"* forms), is NOT tilde-expanded (the '~' is quoted, the word stays RELATIVE) and ASKS, as does a fully-quoted '~'/'~/x', an escaped '\~/...', and an empty-quote-preceded '""~/x' (bash expands only a '~' at the very start of the word). It ALSO ASKS a leading unquoted '~' whose PREFIX itself carries a quote or escape BEFORE the first unquoted '/' - '~"/x"', '~'' (empty single-quote), '~""/x', '~'/x'', '~"/"$V', and a '~' followed by an escaped '/' - because any quote or escape in the tilde-prefix disables bash expansion and the word stays RELATIVE, EVEN when the DECODED token is fully literal '~/x' with no opacity. Only a quote or expansion AFTER the prefix-closing unquoted '/' does not block expansion, so the genuine 'cd ~/$VAR' (prefix is the bare '~', the '$VAR' sits after the '/') STAYS ALLOW. Round-4 propagates this SAME clean-leading-tilde signal into the redirect-TARGET classification (previously the redirect parser discarded it, so a '> ~/x' target was classed opaque and ASKED, inconsistent with 'cd ~/x'): a redirect target whose whole leading tilde-prefix is clean/unquoted now ALLOWS ('> ~/x', '> ~/"x"', '> ~/$V', and the bare '> ~'), while a quoted or complex-prefix tilde target ('> "~"/x', '> ~"/x"') keeps its opacity and ASKS - exactly matching the cd tilde rule. A '~user'/'~user/x' names another account's home whose EXISTENCE the hook cannot verify (an unresolved login name leaves the word RELATIVE), so it is NOT proven absolute and ASKS (the conservative call; a '~user' cd is rare); the '~-'/'~+'/'~N' directory-stack forms likewise ASK. Only the closed option forms are treated as non-destinations, and '--' ENDS option processing, so a genuine relative directory name that begins '-'/'+' is still the destination and ASKS ('cd -- -rel', 'cd +rel', 'cd -rel'), while a lone '-' AFTER '--' is still the $OLDPWD shortcut in bash and ALLOWS ('cd -- -') and a post-'--' directory literally named '--' stays relative and ASKS ('cd -- --'); an opaque '$VAR' destination cannot be proven absolute and ASKS. ANY leading inline env-assignment PREFIXING a cd/pushd (any variable name, '=' or the append '+=' form) can redirect where the cwd-INDEPENDENT destinations land: an inline OLDPWD=/OLDPWD+= redirects the lone '-' ($OLDPWD) shortcut and an inline HOME=/HOME+= redirects the bare 'cd' ($HOME default), in each case to a value the floor cannot prove absolute (e.g. '..'). Round-4 CONSERVATIVE CONSOLIDATION: rather than enumerate OLDPWD/HOME by name (which missed the '+=' append form and the bare-cd HOME default entirely - the round-3 under-blocks), the floor takes the stance that the mere PRESENCE of ANY leading assignment makes those two otherwise-cwd-independent destinations ASK, so 'OLDPWD=.. cd -- -', 'OLDPWD+=.. cd -', 'HOME=.. cd', 'HOME+=.. cd', and 'HOME=.. pushd' all ASK, while a plain zero-assignment 'cd -'/'cd -- -'/bare 'cd' keeps its ALLOW. This is DELIBERATELY conservative in two disclosed ways: (a) a BENIGN leading assignment on a cwd-independent form ('FOO=x cd -', 'FOO=x cd') also ASKS, the accepted cost of not name-enumerating; and (b) an assignment token whose NAME was quoted or escaped ('"OLDPWD"=.. cd -', 'OLD"PWD"=.. cd -', 'OLDP\WD=.. cd -') is a COMMAND to bash (command-not-found; cd never runs), but its DECODED form is assignment-shaped ('OLDPWD=..'), so the floor reads it as a leading assignment and ASKS - an intentional over-fire on an assignment-shaped token bash would reject anyway, NOT chased with assignment-name quote provenance. It reuses the shared quote/redirect-aware lexer (_lex_command), so a redirect anywhere is seen and a quoted metacharacter is not miscounted; but the lexer is NOT a shell interpreter: it cannot resolve an ALIAS, a shell FUNCTION, eval, a command substitution, or a VARIABLE EXPANSION, so a cd or redirect reached through any of those, or whose command word is not literally cd/pushd (a wrapper, a PATH-shadowed name, an absolute /usr/bin/cd is resolved by basename but an aliased 'cd' is not), is not judged. An operand carrying an unexpanded expansion never reads as absolute unless it is literally rooted, so 'cd $DIR' ASKS while 'cd /$X' allows; a redirect target formed from an expansion is classified opaque and ASKS. A bare filename passed to an unknown command is indistinguishable from data and is not judged. Absoluteness is NOT intent: an absolute cd or redirect can still point at the wrong directory. An unparseable construct (a heredoc, here-string, process substitution, '{fd}>' redirect, or an unbalanced quote or escape) is handled by PARTIAL lex: the COMPLETE segments before it AND the positions of the still-open IN-PROGRESS segment that were fully parsed BEFORE it are still inspected, so an earlier resolvable relative cd/redirect - whether in an earlier segment ('cd rel; cat <<EOF...') OR the redirect target of the same in-progress segment parsed before the construct ('cat > out.txt <<EOF...' and 'cat > out.txt <(...)' ASK on out.txt) - still ASKS rather than being discarded; ONLY a cd/redirect position WITHIN or AFTER the unparseable construct is left uninspected and ALLOWED, a disclosed residual rather than an over-ask on every such command. A missing tool_name denies (the shared fail-closed contract); a missing or unreadable command string ASKS rather than silently allowing. It is best-effort against the accidental case, not an adversary, and is platform=claude-code only.

A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string (the shared quote/redirect-aware tokenizer, which REMOVES shell redirection from the token stream, closing the F-122 redirect-pollution class so a redirect before the subcommand, after a refspec-less push, or around --help/-- no longer corrupts the subcommand, operand, or HEAD-probe decision): it judges git push and git commit segments only - the LITERAL commit subcommand; a merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, or rebase that also lands commits on the protected line is out of scope by design, because the accidental case this layer guards is the direct git commit and server-side branch protection remains the real gate. The push layer parses options with a value-skip for the separated value-taking options (--push-option/-o, --repo, --receive-pack/--exec, and --recurse-submodules, whose value is MANDATORY and hence separable - verified against git 2.53.0, which consumes the next token as the value and rejects a bare form) and a --/--end-of-options boundary. Force, delete, sweep, and prune flags are detected VALUE-AWARE inside the token loop, so an option value is never read as a flag (git push -o --force origin main carries a push-option VALUE, not a force flag): every force spelling counts (-f/--force clustered or long, any --force-with-lease spelling - a lease-guarded force still rewrites the remote ref - --force-if-includes, and --mirror, which implies force), plus the ref-sweeping modes: --mirror, a forced --all/--branches, the MATCHING refspec (a bare : pushes every branch existing on both ends and +: is its forced form; either ASKS, a matching-refspec push this guard cannot prove misses the protected branches), and --prune combined with a wildcard or matching refspec (which DELETES every remote branch absent locally with NO force flag - witnessed deleting a remote master - so it ASKS; a --prune whose refspec mapping comes only from configuration falls under the configuration residual below). Operand ROLES follow the grammar git itself uses (git push <repository> <refspec>...): the FIRST bare operand is the repository and is never judged as a destination (a remote literally named main is not a false deny), and only the later, refspec-position operands are judged, by exact case-sensitive DESTINATION name (tolerant of a refs/heads/ or heads/ prefix); a skip-set omission can only shift operands toward over-inclusion, never move a real refspec into the exempt repository slot. A protected DELETION is denied like a force: a --delete or clustered -d flag whose refspec-position operand names a protected branch, and the empty-source :<dst> delete refspec (:main); the deny banner names the actual act, force-push vs branch deletion. When no refspec names a destination (a refspec-less force-push) or the refspec is HEAD/@, the SESSION-CWD current branch is read by a scrubbed read-only symbolic-ref probe (every ambient GIT_* removed, offline, 5s timeout), and a detached or unreadable HEAD reads as UNKNOWN, never as not-protected. Git resolves a pushed or FORCED HEAD/@ to the current branch; a DELETED HEAD or :@ git itself REJECTS as a nonexistent or invalid remote ref, so the probe-backed deny on a deleted HEAD/@ is a harmless safe-direction over-deny kept for uniformity, not a claim that git resolves a deleted HEAD to the current branch. It does NOT catch: a push or commit outside the Bash tool; a git alias or shell function that renames git or expands to a push; a destination supplied by SHELL EXPANSION rather than a literal token (git push --force origin "$BRANCH" with BRANCH holding a protected name, a command substitution, or a glob): a lexical guard judges the literal token and cannot resolve runtime shell state - the same inherent boundary git_discard discloses for its variable and substitution forms; a FRAGMENTED command word or verb (shell quoting that splits the git command word or the push/commit verb so neither the parsed segments nor the raw scan sees a contiguous git-plus-verb keyword; a plain command-word wrapper such as env/sudo/command/xargs IS caught by the raw scan and ASKS); a WRAPPED push in a compound in which ANY other segment, EARLIER OR LATER, parses with git as its command word (git status && sudo git push --force origin main, and equally env git push --force origin main && git status): the benign git segment satisfies the saw-git check, so the wrapped-catch raw scan never runs and the wrapped force-push is silently allowed - an adversarial best-effort residual of the same class as the fragmented command word, disclosed and not chased; a destination supplied by CONFIGURATION rather than the command line (push.default, branch.<name>.pushRemote/merge, remote.<name>.push refspecs, a triangular-push setup), so the bare-push HEAD proxy can diverge from the configured upstream mapping; a protected line under a NON-DEFAULT name (the set ships as main/master); or a rewrite landed on the remote side or by a hosting-provider action (a protected-NAMED force-push or deletion is denied redirect-independently, and a current-branch force-push or deletion under an unresolvable -C/--git-dir/GIT_* redirect ASKS, so none silent-allows). SAFE-DIRECTION OVER-DENIES, accepted and disclosed (re-issue without the contrived flag combination): negation and no-op flags are not modelled, so a --force or --delete cancelled by a later --no-force/--no-delete still denies, --force-if-includes ALONE (a documented no-op without --force-with-lease) denies, and a --dry-run push carrying any force or delete spelling is judged like the real thing and denies. On a shell parse error, OR when a command-word wrapper hides git so no parsed segment resolves to git, it falls back to a conservative raw scan that ASKS (never a hard deny, never a silent allow) on an apparent git force-push (any -f/--force/--for-prefix/--mirror/--all form, or a +refspec anchored to start, whitespace, or either quote character, so a quoted "+main:main" under sudo is caught), an apparent branch deletion (a --de-prefix long flag, or a d carried ANYWHERE in a short - cluster, mirroring the force cluster shape so a wrapped -dv is caught, name-independent like the force spellings; or an empty-source :<protected-name> refspec, judged by its visible name), or an apparent git commit. The raw scan OVER-MATCHES by design (a case-different name, an attached -o value ending in f, an unrelated + or -d token, or prose mentioning the keywords ASKS), so re-issue a wrongly-flagged command as a plain, parseable git command. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it.

gates.residue: Judges only the revision under gate against the derived protected ref: it does not scan the repository's other branches, cannot prove where a branch was originally cut (a branch cut from a sibling that itself descends from the protected line still resolves), passes a fork point that survives a partial rewrite unless the configured lag threshold catches it, does not fail on multiple merge bases, and where no threshold is configured the staleness layer reports and never blocks. With multiple merge bases the reported first-parent lag is the MINIMUM (most-lenient) across bases, so a criss-cross history is judged by its nearest fork point. Replace refs are neutralized in the scrubbed env (GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1) so a `git replace --graft` cannot mask an orphan as rooted through merge-base; the on-disk .git/info/grafts residual is out of scope (an accidental-case guardrail; full adversarial-grade parent-rewrite resistance is not this gate's remit). A shallow repository maps a merge-base miss to cannot-evaluate (exit 2) with a `git fetch --unshallow` remediation, never a false ORPHANED, because truncated history cannot be told from a genuinely absent root (the CI gate checks out at fetch-depth:0). When the protected ref is derived from the default origin/HEAD, a stale local origin/HEAD (not refreshed since the last fetch) can skew the derived protected tip, so both the orphaned and the first-parent-lag verdicts are only as current as the clone's remote-tracking state; pass --protected an authoritative ref, or refresh origin/HEAD, when that currency matters. A degenerate invocation naming the SAME ref for --protected and --head is a self-comparison that always resolves (a ref is rooted on itself); the caller supplies distinct refs. The gate scrubs the ambient GIT_* environment before every git call but resolves the `git` executable through the ambient PATH, so it trusts the toolchain's `git`; a hostile PATH entry shadowing `git` is a trusted-toolchain / execution-environment concern outside this gate's threat model, not a branch-root bypass it defends against.

hooks.residue: Lexical trigger over an open command grammar: a branch created through a wrapper, alias, script, or shell indirection is not seen. When a later construct makes the whole command unparseable (a heredoc, a process substitution), the guard still PARTIAL-lexes and judges the creation recovered in the parseable prefix, so a proven orphan creation followed by an unsupported construct still DENIES (DENY outranks the parse error); only a creation lying ENTIRELY within the unparseable syntax stays unseen (the open-grammar residual), and only creation forms are checked, so switching to an existing orphaned branch, continuing work on the current branch, or RENAMING a branch (-m/-M/--move, which reuses an existing branch's commits under a new name and so creates no new orphan-rootable ref) passes to the CI gate. It probes a creation's ancestry (and can DENY an orphaned start) ONLY for a CLEAN canonical creation: a create trigger (checkout -b/-B; switch -c/-C or --create/--force-create; a bare `git branch <name>`; a `git branch -c/-C/--copy` copy whose start is the SOURCE, an explicit <src> else the current HEAD; or `git worktree add -b/-B`), its operands, and NOTHING ELSE except a tiny allowlist of VALUELESS booleans (--quiet/--force, short q/f; git branch additionally exposes --verbose/-v, which checkout/switch/worktree do not). A confidently-recognized non-creation ACTION (git branch -d/-D/--delete, -m/-M/--move rename, -u/--set-upstream-to/--unset-upstream, --edit-description, --show-current) or a LISTING form (--list, -a/-r/--all/--remotes and the unambiguous listing letters) is ALLOWED. EVERY OTHER shape routes to a fail-SAFE ASK, never a silent allow of a possible creation and never a probe-based DENY of a non-creation: any value-taking option (--contains/--merged/--points-at/--recurse-submodules), any unknown option, any abbreviated (--cre, --orp, --tr) or negated form whose meaning is order- or version-dependent (--no-detach, `--list --no-list`, a clustered -l), any tracking/orphan/detach form (--track/-t/--orphan/--guess/--detach/-d), a copy combined with any non-clean option (git branch --format main -c ...), a bare `git worktree add <path> [<commit-ish>]` without -b, and any short cluster carrying a letter outside the clean/listing set. This MAXIMALLY-CONSERVATIVE posture (maintainer-approved 2026-09-02, after the round-7 simplify-to-ASK cap) trades precision for robustness: an exotic or option-laden git command earns an ASK rather than a precise allow or deny, and the authoritative CI branch-root gate judges the actual post-creation ancestry regardless. DISCLOSED residual: the classifier accepts any nonempty operand as a branch name, so a creation carrying a git-INVALID name (spaces, a `..`, a control character - forms git rejects with `check-ref-format` and creates nothing) can still receive a probe-based deny of that orphaned start; this is a safe-direction false-deny of a no-op command (re-issue with a valid name), and full git ref-name validation is out of this lexical classifier's scope (tracked as HYG-2). What it PROVES at creation time is only that the start point is ORPHANED (no merge base with origin/HEAD); a rooted-but-STALE or old start point (for example checkout -b x origin/HEAD~1) still has a merge base and PASSES this hook, and its staleness is caught only by the CI gate's configured --max-lag first-parent-lag threshold, not here. Replace refs are neutralized on the probe (GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1) so a grafted parent cannot make an orphan look rooted; the on-disk .git/info/grafts residual is out of scope (an accidental-case guardrail). A shallow clone cannot distinguish a missing merge base from unfetched history, so a merge-base miss in a shallow repository routes to ASK, never a deny; a FAILURE of the shallow-status probe itself (a non-zero or unreadable result) likewise routes to ASK, matching the CI gate's cannot-evaluate posture, never a false orphaned deny. A cd/pushd in an earlier segment of the compound command, a non-cosmetic ambient GIT_* variable, or a command-local -C/--git-dir/--work-tree redirect all leave the target repository unreconcilable with the session cwd, so the creation routes to ASK. The ancestry answer comes from the clone's remote-tracking state, which can be stale until the next fetch. The hook derives its PROTECTED ref from the clone's origin/HEAD (the local default-branch pointer), which may differ from the actual protected target the CI gate judges against (the PR base branch): where origin/HEAD points at a non-default branch, the hook can ALLOW a creation the CI gate later reports ORPHANED against the true protected line, since the hook has no PR/target context at creation time; the CI branch-root gate is the authoritative check on the actual post-creation ancestry. The hook resolves the `git` executable through the ambient PATH (a trusted-toolchain boundary, as the sibling gate residue discloses): a hostile PATH entry shadowing `git` could spoof the probe, an adversarial execution-environment concern outside this accidental-case hook's threat model, not a bypass it defends against. The env-assignment command form is best-effort, as for the sibling git hooks. The hook catches only EXPLICIT-start creation forms; an IMPLICIT-start (DWIM) form where git auto-creates a branch from a matching remote-tracking ref (a bare git checkout/switch <name> whose name matches a remote branch, or a --guess/--guess-remote guess) has a start git resolves at runtime and not lexically visible here, so it is routed to ASK where a guess flag is present and otherwise passes the hook and is caught by the authoritative CI branch-root gate, which judges the actual post-creation ancestry.

gates.residue: Total over the surface it examines: an OPEN merge_pending row carrying a TYPED ref (pr:N, decision:X) whose merge or record evidence exists in the declared truth sources always fails the gate. It reads only typed structured refs; a narrative number in prose, an untyped row, or a register kept outside the declared surface is out of scope by design (D9), and drift the truth sources themselves cannot see (an unpushed local merge, a PR merged under a subject with no (#N) marker) passes. In a checkout with no orchestration registry the live leg is NOT APPLICABLE (the record is machine-local by design) and the self-test carries the assurance; that scope boundary is printed, never silent.

hooks.residue: A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string: tokenized with the shared quote/redirect-aware tokenizer (_lex_command), which respects quotes and REMOVES shell redirection from the token stream (so a redirect before or around the subcommand no longer hides a Co-Authored-By trailer, an --author value, or an identity assignment) and grouped into segments on the unquoted shell operators ; | || && & ( ) and newlines, so a subshell-grouped commit (( git commit --author=... )) is judged too, and a trailer hiding inside a quoted -m message (-m "fix; Co-authored-by: Claude", which the old whitespace split broke at the ;) now lives intact in the single message token and is caught by a substring scan on that token. On a git commit-family segment (commit, merge, cherry-pick, am, rebase, revert, commit-tree) it flags a Co-Authored-By trailer inside any token or an --author value (--author=X or --author X) naming an AI; in ANY segment it flags a git-identity env var (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME) or a user.name/user.email value (a -c user.name=X inline or a config user.name X pair) naming an AI, so setting the identity in a prior segment then committing is caught. git global options that take an argument (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --exec-path, --super-prefix, --config-env), whose value is now its own token, are skipped so the value is not misread as the subcommand. The BARE message body is deliberately NOT matched against the identity set: a legitimate message that merely mentions an AI product name (-m "fix claude adapter") records no AI identity, and denying it would be a false positive; only a trailer or an --author value records identity. On a shell parse error (unbalanced quotes) it fails SAFE: a conservative raw-string scan denies an apparent AI trailer/--author/env/config assignment, never a silent-allow. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the common/accidental case (the assistant own accidental violation), not an adversary determined to evade it. It does NOT defeat deliberate shell escaping (git \commit), obfuscation, an alias or function that renames the tool, or persistent shell/env/config state such as an AI identity persisted in git config in a PRIOR TURN (not the same command), a trailer staged into a message file and committed with -F/-t, a commit made outside the Bash tool or the session, or an AI product name outside the recognized identity set.

SessionStart cannot block at the platform (exit 2 shows stderr only, doc-confirmed 2026-08-29), so this layer SURFACES divergence and ARMS the PreToolUse resume barrier; the barrier is the mechanism. Probes, all fail-closed to a finding rather than a silent pass: the declared handoff's Branch line against the real HEAD (scrubbed read-only probe), a handoff gate marker's commit against the real HEAD commit, lease staleness, every declared record surface readable (a declared-but-unreadable surface is a cannot-evaluate FINDING, never nothing-to-check), and merge-pending rows against first-parent merge evidence. Registry-scoped; with no registry it is silent. It reads records and git state only; it cannot detect a handoff that is stale in ways its declared grammar does not carry (free-text drift), and lease MISMATCH detection is bounded to staleness because a session cannot prove its own identity against the holder field.

REGISTRY-SCOPED: entirely inert unless an orchestration registry (.aiqt/orchestration.local.json or .aiqt/orchestration.json) is present AND a declared orchestrator lease or mode record is live, so plain Q&A sessions and bounded workers never inherit the global backlog. FAIL-OPEN on its own I/O errors, none of which wedges the session: an unresolvable cwd or an inactive-or-unreadable lease/mode scope SILENTLY ALLOWS the stop (no warn banner, no guard-event); an unreadable registry ALLOWS with a warn banner but no guard-event; and an unreadable turn-state takes the bounded loop-bound exit. But (FIX 1) an enumerator error or timeout, and any cannot-evaluate (an unreadable proof source), FAIL CLOSED-CONTINUE: the stop is DENIED (ignorance refuses the wind-down), releasable by the operator-owned escape sentinel and never a clean close, bounded by the guard-owned loop bound past which it becomes a deliberate, recorded forced exit. The deny is BOUNDED: the guard's own persisted counter (turn-state, reset on genuine human input) allows at most two denies per epoch, then ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS, independent of any platform loop field (none is documented on Stop; a loop-ish payload field is honoured opportunistically if one ever appears). The operator escape sentinel yields the clean ALLOW only when it passes enforced acceptance: a regular file (never a symlink), owned by a uid other than the guard's effective uid, and not group- or other-writable; a present sentinel failing any condition is IGNORED with the decision unchanged, recorded to guard-events and escape-spoof.json, and surfaced once by the next resume audit. Uid inequality proves not-self, never operator identity; on a shared-uid host no file either party can create passes, so the clean-ALLOW channel is unavailable there (recovery: a differently-owned sentinel such as a root-owned one, operator registry or mode maintenance, or the bounded marked exit; split-uid deployment is the recommended posture). The platform interrupt is a second, structurally unguardable escape, left uncovered on purpose. Blocker proofs are validated against their declared sources (the dispatch ledger, the pending-decisions surface, evidence freshness, the clock), but that whole substantiation surface (the backlog state/granted fields, a pending-decision row, the dispatch ledger, a not-before value, and free-text external evidence) is largely ACTOR-AUTHORABLE: the guard raises the bar (it rejects an unknown blocker kind and requires a substantiating record in the declared authoritative source) yet cannot categorically enforce that a block is granted by an authority other than the assistant, closed categorically only by operator-owned, assistant-non-writable records at the OS layer (SYSTEM-HARDENING.md entry 2). Plausibly FABRICATED external evidence in particular is not mechanically closable at this layer where no attestation register is declared; where one is declared, an external or foreign-lease blocker classifies blocked only when its ref is covered by a fresh validated attestation whose snapshot is re-anchored to the register authority and whose refs are re-derived from the register content at yield, so a swapped register or a fabricated-refs snapshot substantiates nothing; this raises the bar over free-text evidence but is not categorically forgery-proof, since the register is a separately-declared surface and filesystem write to it, wherever it is declared, forges an attestation by appending a valid approved row (uncommitted; the git or anchor authority checks only the committed or anchored prefix), closed categorically only by an operator-owned, assistant-non-writable register at the OS layer; the remaining residuals are cadence, since tamper misleads until the next audit or gate run, and relevance, since a resolving pointer can still be a misappropriated pretext that triage refutes). The human-decision class proves only that a pending-decision row exists, never that the item genuinely crosses the human-oversight threshold, which stays human judgement. Rather than ENUMERATE every dumping form of git (an unbounded shell + git-option grammar, GD-34/F-119), the ALLOW path PROVES the safe form: a git diff-PRODUCER is ALLOWED only when the WHOLE command matches one of FIVE closed proofs. (A) EXACT help: a metacharacter-free git <producer> --help or -h (and the exact git stash show --help/-h). (B) EXACT summary-only: a metacharacter-free single simple command (a conservative character set of letters, digits, space, tab, and _ - . / = : @ , + % and no shell reserved word), whose first resolved words are literally git and a summary-capable producer (diff/show/range-diff/log/diff-tree/diff-index/diff-files, plus the explicit git stash show), carrying at least one EXACT summary selector (--stat/--shortstat/--numstat/--name-only/--name-status) before a --/--end-of-options boundary and no other option-like word before the boundary except an exact --no-patch (bare operands allowed). (C) DIRECT static real-file diversion: a SINGLE simple command whose command word is literally git, a possible producer, with no opaque shell feature, whose FINAL stdout redirect (last-redirect-wins over the raw redirect metadata) is proven to land on a static non-/dev,/proc file - supporting leading, interspersed, and trailing redirects, but never a dynamic target (a variable, command substitution, or tilde), a descriptor duplication (1>&2, or a 3>out 1>&3 fd-graph, classified opaque), or a /dev,/proc target. (D) EXACT terminal pager pipeline: a plain literal unwrapped git producer, an exact | (not |&), then exactly one bare pager word (less/more/most/pager) with no options, operands, or redirection and no later pipe. (E) BENIGN git log listing: a metacharacter-free single simple command whose first words are literally git and log, every option before a --/--end-of-options boundary drawn from an EXACT allowlist of VALUE-FREE, provably-diff-free display/traversal flags (--oneline, --graph, --decorate, --no-decorate, --abbrev-commit, --reverse, --all) with bare revision/pathspec operands allowed - a plain commit listing that provably emits no diff (git log renders a patch ONLY with a patch flag, and a summary --stat form is already proof B). A git log carrying ANY other flag - a patch flag, a pickaxe -G/-S (whose diff output depends on a co-present -p), a summary/file-list flag (--numstat/--shortstat/--name-only/--name-status, which are the proof-B summary escape, allowed there like git diff --name-only), a value-taking option such as --format/-n <count>/--author=/--since=/--grep=, or any unknown flag - is NOT admitted by proof E and routes to the default (ASK, or DENY on a confirmed patch). The ALLOW path DELIBERATELY does NOT parse the full git/shell option grammar. Every OTHER possible producer is ASK or DENY: a producer CONFIRMED to emit a console patch (a default diff/show/range-diff, a patch-flagged listing, a summary token in a NON-option position such as git diff -- --stat, a producer piped into a known console/truncating sink cat/tee/head/tail, or a stdout redirect to /dev,/proc) and fitting no proof DENIES; any other producer-capable-but-unproven form ASKS. A producer that diverts its output with --output/-o writes the diff to THAT target, not stdout, so a shell redirect or a pager is a DECOY: proofs C and D do not apply, a --output to a /dev,/proc console DENIES, and a --output to a file or a dynamic target ASKS. A command word this guard cannot resolve to a literal git (an ANSI-C dollar-single-quote form or a $VAR expansion) beside a producer surface is never proven benign and never a CONFIRMED console dump: it ASKS. Across a compound or multiple producers, DENY outranks ASK, and a multi-command form is NEVER allowed merely because one segment is safe. The possible-producer scope is BROAD (a git word followed by a producer surface in the cleaned argv, robust to quote fragmentation, OR a raw-text probe that over-matches quoted prose), so it OVER-ASKS by design; on a tokenizer parse failure (an unbalanced quote or an unsupported construct such as a heredoc or process substitution) an apparent producer ASKS - never a silent allow, and no summary or redirect regex can earn an ALLOW from an unparseable command. DELIBERATE OVER-ASKS, disclosed: a wrapper (env/sudo/command git diff), a pathed git (/usr/bin/git show), a leading assignment, any quote in a would-be summary command, a git log carrying any extra or unknown flag OUTSIDE the proof-E benign set (git log -5, git log -G/-S, git log --format, git log --author=), git grep diff, an extra summary modifier (git diff -M --stat, git diff -S --stat, git diff --stat=80), a compound, and quoted prose (an echo of the literal text git diff) all ASK rather than risk a false ALLOW. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the common/accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it.

gates.residue: An adopter-parameterized scan that flags a hardcoded LITERAL value at an adopter-declared command sink (a command word plus an option name in a declared command-surface file), so a reusable command derives its target-specific parameter rather than baking one in (grdinp input-soundness, exetgt templated-target re-verification). hooks.residue: A PATH guard, not a content judge: it decides where a write lands, never what it writes. Covers only PreToolUse Write, Edit, and MultiEdit calls carrying a readable file_path. TWO arming inputs, each fail-open on genuine ABSENCE only: the per-slice declaration write-scope.json, read at the orchestration registry-declared state_dir (resolved from the registry the guard reads EXACTLY ONCE, via the pure _state_dir_from_registry helper, never a second independently-faulting read; out of the slice tree by default but MAY be in-tree when the registry declares an in-tree state_dir), arms SLICE CONFINEMENT; the in-tree committed frozen floor .aiqt/frozen.json (generated by tools/gen_manifest.py from the ownership classification, drift-gated) arms the FROZEN layer. The structural other-repo/nested-repo denial applies to every covered write whose repository root resolves; the frozen-floor denial fires whenever a floor is PRESENT, and an armed session additionally requires one, so neither is unconditionally always-on and only an un-armed session with a genuinely-absent floor leaves the frozen layer inert. Slice confinement is fail-open on a missing declaration. The principled fail-open is genuine ABSENCE (of a declaration or floor: no confinement in effect, the same inert boundary gensrc and the orchestration suite use); a cannot-evaluate FAULT is not absence and denies (see the fail posture below). The registry that LOCATES the declaration is part of the read: a bad or unreadable registry (an lstat fault, a read/parse error, a non-version-1 object, or a present-but-malformed state_dir) is a cannot-evaluate that DENIES rather than silently falling back to XDG and disarming confinement. Out-of-scope is a DENY, never an ASK (an ASK would hand the confined actor the click-through on its own confinement and would wedge an unattended run); the remedy is the harness re-declaring the slice, so scope-widening stays on the harness side, never a guarded-tool call. The declaration is machine-set inert data, never authored by the assistant through a guarded tool; the residual Bash-write path to the state dir remains, so the harness-set integrity is defence in depth, not categorical. Fail posture, by regime: a MISSING tool_name denies (the shared fail-closed contract); a malformed tool_name, an unreadable tool_input, a missing/empty file_path, or a control-character file_path denies as a malformed call in either regime; a covered write whose session repository root cannot be resolved (a missing/unreadable cwd or a non-git session) DENIES fail-closed in both regimes, because the root is resolved FIRST and containment cannot be evaluated without it, so this denial precedes any relative-path handling (a non-git relative-path write DENIES, it does not defer); only WHEN the root resolves does an un-armed relative file_path defer to the sibling absolute_paths hook (which owns the relative case, EN-8 making no cwd-trusting determination) and allow, while an armed relative file_path denies; an un-armed realpath/containment/nested-repo-probe FAULT now DENIES too (a cannot-evaluate: the guard cannot prove the target is in-repo and not nested, so it denies rather than allowing an unverified write), as the same fault does armed; a target proven OUTSIDE the session toplevel, or in a NESTED or FOREIGN git repository under or beside it (resolved via the scrubbed git toplevel of the target nearest existing ancestor, every ambient GIT_* removed so a decoy repo cannot redirect the read), denies in BOTH regimes; a present frozen floor with the target on it denies in both regimes (the floor outranks the allowlist, deny over allow), a present-but-malformed floor denies (cannot-evaluate), and an ABSENT floor is inert un-armed but denies while armed (an armed session must commit a floor, an explicit empty list being valid, so a Bash-deleted floor cannot silently downgrade an armed session); armed, a declaration that is unreadable, malformed, unknown-version, or whose worktree_root does not resolve to this repo (a stale, copied, or moved declaration) denies; an allow entry wholly on the frozen floor makes the declaration malformed and denies (a declaration cannot declare past the floor); a target in repo, not frozen, and in the declared slice scope allows silently, while one not in scope denies. Every deny attempts a BEST-EFFORT guard-events append (the over-fire metric) where the root is resolvable: the append can fail silently (_orch_append_jsonl returns False and the deny ignores it), which neither blocks nor alters the denial and may lose the over-fire metric for that event. Matching is on canonicalized real paths with component-boundary tree containment (the gensrc idiom), never a raw string prefix; the declaration and floor share one entry grammar (a repo-root-relative POSIX path, a trailing / marks a tree, no absolute/backslash/./../control-char/wildcard component). The floor is enforced against the manifest CLASS set {derived, manifest-self, archive}. The RUNTIME value of that floor is un-lowerable by the constrained actor through the guarded tools (a guarded write to .aiqt/frozen.json is itself on the floor and denied); but its DEFINITION (FROZEN_CLASSES in tools/gen_manifest.py) is generator source that lands through pull-request review PLUS the drift gate, which detects an INCONSISTENT floor (a committed frozen.json that does not match a fresh regeneration), NOT an unauthorized-but-internally-consistent redefinition of the class set followed by regeneration; an independent floor-authorization mechanism is out of scope for this hook. The floor proves membership in its declared selector set only, not that the generation-time class mapping is semantically complete. Class c (partial), matching the sibling gensrc_guard: the control fires deterministically inside its Write|Edit|MultiEdit matcher, but the rules it enforces span write paths the matcher cannot see (Bash-mediated writes, NotebookEdit, filesystem MCP tools, any write outside the platform hook path), and its slice-arming state is machine-local, so CI cannot observe the confinement. The committed frozen floor .aiqt/frozen.json is a generated, drift-gated output backstopped at merge by the manifest-gen-drift gate (tools/gen_manifest.py --check), the gensrc-registry-drift gate (tools/gen_gensrc.py --check), and the independent manifest-integrity verifier (tools/check_manifest.py) (defence in depth, each catching the other residual; these CI gates are not removed or softened), but nothing backstops an uncommitted, out-of-scope-mutable, or cross-repository write through the uncovered channels. Realpath closes symlink escapes present at check time but not a post-check swap, hard-link alias, bind-mount change, or case-fold/Unicode alias between the lstat probe and the tool write (TOCTOU); an OS-level write sandbox is the stronger overlapping control where available. It is single-author by design: exactly one declaration, one writer, harness-replaced; it is confinement of the sole writer, not parallel-write collision arbitration.

gates.residue: Token-level set parity between the two named files only (tools/run_all_checks.sh and .github/workflows/quality.yml), read as data and never executed. Identity is the normalized command including all script arguments, with python/shell launcher words and the interpreter-only flags (-I, -B, -E, -s, -P, -u, glued forms included) removed, and the value of a runtime-derived flag (--base, --protected, --head) masked as <ref:expression> (preserving which expression supplied it) only when it carries a shell expansion or GitHub expression, so a change among runtime spellings including a self-comparison diverges, while a literal value stays in identity and two different literals diverge. It does NOT compare environment values, operating systems, tool versions, execution order, multiplicity, step placement across jobs, labels, or whether the shell harness propagates a child failure; interpreter-flag differences are owned by check_python_launcher_isolation.py. Scope is exactly the two files, so gates in other workflows are not enumerated. Argument order is identity-relevant, so a harmless reorder fails loud. Coordinated removal of both of this gate's own invocations is undetectable if nobody runs the remaining file manually (branch protection and review own that case). The extractors implement a disclosed shell and YAML subset; an unknown construct is cannot-evaluate (exit 2), never a clean pass. The `default` is "ask" because the recoverable ask is the characteristic behaviour; a confirmed whole-tree loss on a probed-dirty tree DENIES (unless the leading opt-out is set), BUT under a non-cosmetic ambient GIT_* var (an unresolvable repository view) even a whole-tree clobber ASKS with a best-effort cwd snapshot instead, because the guard cannot prove the target IS the session tree. It fails open (ALLOW) ONLY at the true boundary - a command with no git command-word, no recognized lossy verb, or an unparseable command (a tokenizer ValueError) that names no lossy verb keyword - because that is not a discard it can reason about. WITHIN scope (a recognized lossy verb: checkout/switch/restore/reset/clean/stash/rm/branch) the outcome is ASK UNLESS the command is a PRISTINE SINGLE BARE `git <verb>` invocation AND (for a lossy form) the whole working tree is PROVABLY CLEAN, or the LEADING opt-out is set, or the form is genuinely non-destructive, in which cases ALLOW. PRISTINE SINGLE BARE is judged PURELY LEXICALLY (the bash grammar is NEVER parsed): after optional leading KEY=value assignments the command is exactly `git <args>` as ONE simple command, and the RAW string carries NO shell metacharacter ANYWHERE, EVEN INSIDE QUOTES - none of `;` `|` `&` `<` `>` `(` `)` `{` `}` `$` backtick backslash `!` newline, which by construction also rules out `&&`/`||`/`|&`, EVERY redirection form (`>`, `>>`, `<`, `2>`, `&>`, `>&`, `n>&m`, a leading or interspersed redirect), and EVERY command/process substitution (backtick, `$( )`, `<( )`, `>( )`) - AND no shell reserved word (if/then/elif/else/fi/for/while/until/do/done/case/esac/function/select/`[[`/`]]`/`{`/`}`) AND a command word that is LITERALLY `git` (not a path like /usr/bin/git, and not a wrapper: command/exec/builtin/env/xargs/time/`!`/sudo/nice/timeout/nohup/sh -c/bash -c).
