There is NO claim that any compound, wrapped, redirected, or non-pristine form the guard RECOGNIZES as in-scope is proven safe: those are never ALLOWED, only ASKED (a pristine bare form carrying the leading opt-out is the sole override, short-circuiting even the redirect gate); the one exception is a wrapper that fragments the command word `git` or the verb so no recognized lossy verb is seen (a disclosed residual below), which reads as out-of-scope and is silently ALLOWED, not ASKED. A dirty tree ALONE does not force that outcome on a PRISTINE bare form: a dirty-tree WHOLE-TREE clobber DENIES and other non-pristine or redirected forms ASK, but a genuinely non-destructive form (reset --soft, plain switch, checkout -b, clean -n) can still ALLOW on a dirty tree when no redirect, opt-out, or ambient override applies. Verb forms (each ALLOWs only as a pristine bare command on a provably-clean tree, or one carrying the leading opt-out, except the unconditional-allow and unconditional-ask forms noted): checkout - a plain unforced branch-create (-b/--orphan) with NO merge option is an unconditional allow (git carries changes and aborts on conflict), and the NEW-BRANCH NAME argument of -b/-B (attached -bfoo or separated -b foo) is parsed as that name, never char-scanned as clustered force flags, so -bfoo/-bBranch ALLOW and are never mis-read as carrying -f/-B (F-85); -B is a force branch-create/RESET that overwrites an existing branch ref and can orphan committed commits, so it ASKS (including when combined with other flags); a -m/--merge or --conflict[=<style>] merge-switch, WITH or WITHOUT a -b create, does a three-way merge that can overwrite local changes and is worktree-scoped, decided before the branch-create allow (F-88); -p/--patch, any pathspec/bare-operand form, or a forced -f -b branch-create is worktree-scoped; -f with no pathspec is a whole-tree clobber. switch - -f/--force/--discard-changes is a clobber; -C/--force-create is a force branch-create/RESET that overwrites an existing branch ref and can orphan committed commits, so it ASKS; --merge/-m and --conflict[=<style>] are worktree-scoped (a three-way merge can overwrite local changes); a plain switch or an unforced -c create with NO merge option preserves non-conflicting local changes and aborts rather than lose them, so it is an unconditional allow, and the NEW-BRANCH NAME argument of -c/-C (attached -cfoo or separated -c foo) is parsed as that name, never char-scanned as clustered force flags, so -cfeature ALLOWs and is never mis-read as carrying -f/-C (F-85). restore - EVERY form is worktree-scoped, including --staged (it can erase staged-only content). reset - effective --hard clobbers; --soft is an unconditional allow (HEAD-only, index and worktree intact); --merge/--mixed/--keep/path-scoped/no-mode are scoped (index-changing); an ambiguous bare --m is scoped. rm - EVERY form is worktree-scoped, including --cached. clean - ANY non-dry-run clean is an unconditional ASK (untracked files are a different, unrecoverable asset, and the guard does not model whether the clean would fire, closing the clean.requireForce/-q/-i/clustered-flag edges); a -n/--dry-run judged before any `--` allows, BUT when an arg-consuming option -e/--exclude is present the `-n` is not trusted (it may be the exclude pattern) so the clean routes to its ASK. Destructive options are matched by CONSERVATIVE PREFIX (--patc=--patch, --del=--delete, --dis=--discard-changes, --har=--hard, --mer=--merge are unambiguous abbreviations git accepts; an AMBIGUOUS force-prefix like --for, which git itself REJECTS for branch as ambiguous with --format and for switch as ambiguous with --force-create, is treated as force ANYWAY, erring safe rather than recognizing only spellings git would accept); a `--`/`--end-of-options` boundary is respected so an operand after it (git clean -f -- -nasty, git rm -f -- --cached) is a pathspec, never a safe-looking option. stash drop/clear ASK, and stash export ASK for every spelling (F-95: export writes stash state to a ref, and --to-ref overwrites an arbitrary ref unconditionally); branch force forms ASK - -D/--delete --force (force delete), -M/--move --force (force rename), -C/--copy --force (force copy), -f/--force with an operand (force reset), and a delete (-d/-D/--delete) combined with -r/--remotes (F-94: deleting remote-tracking refs, which git force-removes past the merged-branch safeguard) - while a plain create/list, a local non-remotes -d, and an unforced -m/-c stay allow, and an attached -u<upstream> value (-ufoo, -u <upstream>) is parsed as the upstream, never scanned as a clustered force flag. A `git -C <dir> ...` or a GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE-prefixed form is pristine-lexically but names a worktree the guard cannot resolve to the session cwd, so it ASKS (unless the leading opt-out is set, evaluated before this redirect gate) rather than trust a session-dir probe. An AMBIENT GIT_*-prefixed var in the process env also forces ASK unless it is one of a small COSMETIC allowlist (UI/editor/pager/prompt/lock/identity vars that cannot change the discard target, the object/ref view, the index, or dirtiness detection): the probe scrubs every ambient GIT_* and reads the real cwd repo, but the guard cannot scrub them from the ACTUAL command, which still inherits them and may act on a different git dir, work tree, index, or object/ref view, so the guard cannot prove the repository view the ACTUAL command uses IS the session cwd. Under any such non-cosmetic ambient var EVERY in-scope pristine form ASKS (unless the leading opt-out is set, which is evaluated even earlier and short-circuits this gate) - a destructive clobber AND an otherwise-non-destructive allow form (reset --soft, plain switch, clean -n, checkout -b) alike, checked BEFORE the role/allow logic - each with a best-effort cwd snapshot WHEN the session cwd is a not-provably-clean snappable tree (no usable session cwd, a provably-clean cwd, or a stash/branch-only form, takes none; the snapshot may not capture a redirected tree), so no allow form and no clean cwd probe wins a silent ALLOW under such a redirect. A GIT_TRACE* var is NOT cosmetic: an absolute GIT_TRACE value makes the ACTUAL command append trace output to that path (which could be a repo file), so it too forces ASK, unless the leading opt-out is set (the recovery/probe git calls still scrub the whole GIT_TRACE family per round 6, so THEY write no trace, but the ambient GIT_TRACE on the command itself is not neutralized). This is FAIL-SAFE by construction rather than a fixed enumeration (which kept missing new members - GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE, GIT_REFERENCE_BACKEND - and more will exist): an unknown or new non-cosmetic GIT_* var ASKS rather than winning a silent ALLOW. This control is SIDE-EFFECTING (EN-6 recovery layer): before it ALLOWS or ASKS a snapshottable in-scope discard (checkout/switch/restore/reset/rm/clean) whose worktree it can resolve to the session cwd AND whose tree is NOT provably clean, it takes an INERT recovery snapshot of the uncommitted work and appends one line to an EXTERNAL per-user ledger, so a discard that is asked-then-approved OR wrongly allowed by a mis-parse is still recoverable (the hook fires once, with no post-approval callback). F-D EXPANSION: a NON-PRISTINE in-scope ASK (a compound, wrapped, or redirected snapshottable command) is ALSO snapshot-backed BEST-EFFORT against the SESSION CWD repo, so an asked-then-approved wrapped discard is recoverable too; because the redirected dir of a non-pristine command is NOT parsed, a command that changes into a DIFFERENT repository may be snapshotted at the session repo rather than the target (a same-repo cd is still captured by the whole-tree `git add --all`), and on snapshot fail the decision stays ASK. The snapshot uses a TEMPORARY GIT_INDEX_FILE outside the repo (seeded by copying the real index), `git add --all` (captures tracked-modified + UNTRACKED; ignored excluded), `git write-tree`, `git commit-tree` (parent = HEAD when present), and a CREATE-ONLY `git update-ref refs/aiqt-recovery/<utc-ts>-<pid> <sha>` with an empty expected-old value (a name collision FAILS the snapshot rather than clobbering a prior recovery ref). The snapshot writes only git objects and one private ref (plus a reflog entry for it when core.logAllRefUpdates=always, or when a reflog already exists for the ref) and does NOT itself touch the real index, worktree, HEAD, or any branch; the ref is invisible to plain `git status`, `git branch`, and `git log` but is reachable via `git log --all` / `git for-each-ref refs/aiqt-recovery` / `git show-ref` (a real ref, not hidden). Every real-state git call in this control takes an ALLOWLIST posture, scrubbing EVERY ambient GIT_*-prefixed var rather than enumerating a family (rounds 4-5 kept finding new members: GIT_CONFIG_*, then GIT_TRACE*, then GIT_ATTR_SOURCE), so an ambient decoy repo (GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE), an ambient `git -c` (GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS) config injection, an ambient GIT_ATTR_SOURCE attribute-source redirect, or an ambient GIT_TRACE that would make a read-only call WRITE a trace file cannot reach these calls; the scrub itself re-asserts GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (so the scrub cannot strip the offline + non-interactive posture: no partial-clone lazy-fetch over the network, no prompting) plus a FIXED INTERNAL recovery identity (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=aiqt-recovery, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=aiqt-recovery@localhost) so the snapshot `git commit-tree` never depends on an ambient or on-disk user.name/user.email the scrub removed - which would make it FAIL where no git identity is configured (a CI runner or fresh install with no global gitconfig), silently disabling the recovery backstop - and a recovery commit is deterministically attributed to the guard, not the user, the callers re-apply only the few vars they set themselves AFTER the scrub (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS for the read-only probe, a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE for a snapshot), and any GIT_* the call genuinely needed but was scrubbed fails SAFE to a probe/snapshot failure (fail-to-ASK, never a silent allow). This closes the whole ambient-env class at once; the residual is NOT limited to on-disk config - it spans the non-GIT_ environment (HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/PATH/TMPDIR), on-disk git configuration AND attributes (repo/global/system .gitconfig and .gitattributes), index and ignore state, submodules and embedded repos, configured hooks and filters, PATH-based git resolution, and partial-clone object availability, all read by git by design. RESIDUAL (the honest bound on "inert"): the inert guarantee is BOUNDED, not categorical, because git may ADDITIONALLY run a git-configured (repo, global, system, or command-scope) program during the snapshot whose effect is outside this guard control - a clean/process filter runs on `git add --all` (the CHECK-IN / clean direction, NOT smudge, which would run only on a restore/checkout), an fsmonitor hook runs on the `git status` probe, and a reference-transaction hook plus a post-index-change hook can run on the temp-index write and on the `git update-ref`; a clean filter can TRANSFORM the captured bytes, so the snapshot is NOT guaranteed byte-exact on a filtered repo; and a single overlaid tree cannot capture dirty content inside a SUBMODULE or an untracked EMBEDDED git repo (it stores only the gitlink) and flattens staged-vs-unstaged into ONE tree. The ledger is `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/aiqt-guardrails/recovery.jsonl` (normally outside the repo, so a `git clean` cannot destroy it). The ledger write is BEST-EFFORT: normally one line per snapshot, but skipped when no per-user location resolves (absent HOME/XDG), when that path would resolve inside the repo, or when the directory or write fails. A written line records: utc ts, repo path, the triggering git VERB (never the raw command or file contents), the recovery ref, the snapshot sha, the covered classes (tracked/staged/untracked), and the exact restore command (`git checkout <ref> -- :/`, OVERLAY mode: it brings back modified and new content but does NOT re-apply a recorded file deletion; for an exact, deletion-inclusive restore use an isolated branch via `git switch -c aiqt-recover-<id> <ref>`). The snapshot is decision-INDEPENDENT (it does not trust the form-classifier), so it also fires on a genuinely-safe snapshottable form (reset --soft, plain switch, checkout -b, clean -n) on a dirty tree, an accepted over-snapshot; it is SKIPPED on a provably-clean tree, out of scope, and for stash/branch (a worktree snapshot cannot capture stash entries or branch commits). FAIL POSTURE: when a warranted snapshot cannot be made (probe/write error, an undecodable non-UTF-8 path, over a ~100 MiB changed-content size cap, a bare or broken git dir, or a temp dir resolving inside the repo) it NEVER becomes a silent allow of a not-provably-clean discard - a would-be ALLOW is DOWNGRADED to ASK ("no recovery point could be created"), and an already-ASK/DENY decision is left as-is with the failure surfaced. Retention is NOT handled here (refs accumulate; auto-pruning is a separate maintenance op, never inside PreToolUse). An explicit GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD truthy assignment (anything but "", "0", "false", "no", "off"; an empty final assignment `GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=` is falsy by bash last-wins and does NOT opt out) LEADING a pristine bare git command (the documented `GUARDRAIL_ALLOW_DISCARD=1 git ...` prefix, not the same string buried in an argument nor on a non-pristine/compound command) opts out to ALLOW: being an explicit override in which the operator takes full responsibility, it is evaluated FIRST and short-circuits ALL of the gates below for that pristine form - the command-local-redirect/ambient view-uncertainty gate, the dirty-tree DENY, and the recovery layer alike - so an opt-out discard is NOT snapshot-backed, and a non-pristine form is never rescued by it (the opt-out is honoured only on a pristine single bare command). On an UNPARSEABLE command (a tokenizer ValueError) the opt-out is NOT honoured at all: the guard cannot parse the command, so it cannot soundly trust an opt-out-looking prefix inside it, and an unparseable in-scope command ALWAYS ASKS. HONEST RESIDUAL: being a LEXICAL hook it does NOT catch a git alias (config-defined; an inline `-c alias.<name>=...` now ASKS) or shell function that renames git or expands to a work-losing verb, a discard performed OUTSIDE the Bash tool, or persistent shell/config state set in a PRIOR turn. It also does NOT catch a real discard whose VERB is OUTSIDE the recognized set AND unflagged by the raw scan: a `git worktree remove -f` (or `--force`) of a dirty linked worktree discards the uncommitted work in that worktree, but `worktree` matches no lossy keyword, so the command is allowed at the true boundary; that verb is deliberately NOT added this round (disclosure matches the best-effort posture). By contrast (F-97), a command the raw scan DOES flag as in-scope whose resolved subcommand is nonetheless outside the recognized set (`git checkout-index -a -f`, `git read-tree -u --reset HEAD`, flagged by their `checkout`/`reset` substring) is NO LONGER silently allowed - it ASKS, since a flagged sub the classifier cannot resolve to a known verb cannot be proven non-destructive, and its sub is not snapshottable so no recovery point exists. It also does NOT catch deliberate token fragmentation or obfuscation of the COMMAND WORD `git` ITSELF or of the verb: a wrapper whose git command word or verb is SPLIT by shell quoting so neither the token scan nor the raw scan sees a contiguous git+work-losing keyword (a wrapped, quote-fragmented reset such as env git followed by a quote-broken re-set, or a command word quote-broken so it spells git only after the shell strips the quotes (a quote-broken git under a wrapper such as command or env), whose raw string carries no contiguous `git`+`reset`) reads as "no recognized lossy verb" and is silently ALLOWED, so the claim that any wrapper ASKS is NOT categorical: it holds only while the raw scan still sees a contiguous git+verb keyword. This is a disclosed best-effort residual, not chased (the guard targets the accidental case, not an adversary deliberately splitting the command word or the verb). The probe ITSELF can be made to under-report dirtiness by git config or index state: an `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` mark on a tracked file, or a `submodule.<name>.ignore` setting, hides real modifications from `git status`, so the guard can read a genuinely-dirty tree as provably clean and ALLOW a discard of that hidden work; and the recovery snapshot ALSO cannot capture assume-unchanged/skip-worktree content (it is not in what `git add --all` re-stages) nor IGNORED files (git add --all excludes them; an ignored file overwritten by a forced checkout or removed by `clean -x` is unprobed - to avoid asking on every repo carrying build artifacts - and unsnapshotted). Beyond that, being ultra-conservative it OVER-ASKS heavily - every compound, wrapped, redirected, or metacharacter-bearing command that names a lossy verb ASKS even when it would have been safe (a pristine bare form carrying the leading opt-out is the sole override, short-circuiting even the redirect gate), and a command that merely CONTAINS a git token and a lossy verb as TEXT while running no discard (`echo git branch`, `git log | grep branch`) ASKS too, because the raw scan matches the keywords wherever they appear (a safe-direction over-ask, not narrowed: narrowing the raw scan is the whack-a-mole GD-34 rejected), and a pristine whole-tree clobber over-DENIES on a dirty tree even when the specific target would have lost nothing - an accepted, recoverable cost of never silently allowing a real WORKING-TREE-CONTENT discard for a recognized command that is NOT covered by the explicit leading opt-out or a disclosed residual. That no-silent-allow guarantee is bounded to working-tree content: ref-level moves (reset --soft moving HEAD, a merged-branch delete) are reflog-recoverable, and the obfuscation/config residuals above are best-effort, not categorical.

A best-effort QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check over the Bash command string (the shared quote/redirect-aware tokenizer, which REMOVES shell redirection from the token stream, closing the F-122 redirect-pollution class so a redirect before the subcommand, after a refspec-less push, or around --help/-- no longer corrupts the subcommand, operand, or HEAD-probe decision): it judges git push and git commit segments only - the LITERAL commit subcommand; a merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, or rebase that also lands commits on the protected line is out of scope by design, because the accidental case this layer guards is the direct git commit and server-side branch protection remains the real gate. The push layer parses options with a value-skip for the separated value-taking options (--push-option/-o, --repo, --receive-pack/--exec, and --recurse-submodules, whose value is MANDATORY and hence separable - verified against git 2.53.0, which consumes the next token as the value and rejects a bare form) and a --/--end-of-options boundary. Force, delete, sweep, and prune flags are detected VALUE-AWARE inside the token loop, so an option value is never read as a flag (git push -o --force origin main carries a push-option VALUE, not a force flag): every force spelling counts (-f/--force clustered or long, any --force-with-lease spelling - a lease-guarded force still rewrites the remote ref - --force-if-includes, and --mirror, which implies force), plus the ref-sweeping modes: --mirror, a forced --all/--branches, the MATCHING refspec (a bare : pushes every branch existing on both ends and +: is its forced form; either ASKS, a matching-refspec push this guard cannot prove misses the protected branches), and --prune combined with a wildcard or matching refspec (which DELETES every remote branch absent locally with NO force flag - witnessed deleting a remote master - so it ASKS; a --prune whose refspec mapping comes only from configuration falls under the configuration residual below). Operand ROLES follow the grammar git itself uses (git push <repository> <refspec>...): the FIRST bare operand is the repository and is never judged as a destination (a remote literally named main is not a false deny), and only the later, refspec-position operands are judged, by exact case-sensitive DESTINATION name (tolerant of a refs/heads/ or heads/ prefix); a skip-set omission can only shift operands toward over-inclusion, never move a real refspec into the exempt repository slot. A protected DELETION is denied like a force: a --delete or clustered -d flag whose refspec-position operand names a protected branch, and the empty-source :<dst> delete refspec (:main); the deny banner names the actual act, force-push vs branch deletion. When no refspec names a destination (a refspec-less force-push) or the refspec is HEAD/@, the SESSION-CWD current branch is read by a scrubbed read-only symbolic-ref probe (every ambient GIT_* removed, offline, 5s timeout), and a detached or unreadable HEAD reads as UNKNOWN, never as not-protected. Git resolves a pushed or FORCED HEAD/@ to the current branch; a DELETED HEAD or :@ git itself REJECTS as a nonexistent or invalid remote ref, so the probe-backed deny on a deleted HEAD/@ is a harmless safe-direction over-deny kept for uniformity, not a claim that git resolves a deleted HEAD to the current branch. It does NOT catch: a push or commit outside the Bash tool; a git alias or shell function that renames git or expands to a push; a destination supplied by SHELL EXPANSION rather than a literal token (git push --force origin "$BRANCH" with BRANCH holding a protected name, a command substitution, or a glob): a lexical guard judges the literal token and cannot resolve runtime shell state - the same inherent boundary git_discard discloses for its variable and substitution forms; a FRAGMENTED command word or verb (shell quoting that splits the git command word or the push/commit verb so neither the parsed segments nor the raw scan sees a contiguous git-plus-verb keyword; a plain command-word wrapper such as env/sudo/command/xargs IS caught by the raw scan and ASKS); a WRAPPED push in a compound in which ANY other segment, EARLIER OR LATER, parses with git as its command word (git status && sudo git push --force origin main, and equally env git push --force origin main && git status): the benign git segment satisfies the saw-git check, so the wrapped-catch raw scan never runs and the wrapped force-push is silently allowed - an adversarial best-effort residual of the same class as the fragmented command word, disclosed and not chased; a destination supplied by CONFIGURATION rather than the command line (push.default, branch.<name>.pushRemote/merge, remote.<name>.push refspecs, a triangular-push setup), so the bare-push HEAD proxy can diverge from the configured upstream mapping; a protected line under a NON-DEFAULT name (the set ships as main/master); or a rewrite landed on the remote side or by a hosting-provider action (a protected-NAMED force-push or deletion is denied redirect-independently, and a current-branch force-push or deletion under an unresolvable -C/--git-dir/GIT_* redirect ASKS, so none silent-allows). SAFE-DIRECTION OVER-DENIES, accepted and disclosed (re-issue without the contrived flag combination): negation and no-op flags are not modelled, so a --force or --delete cancelled by a later --no-force/--no-delete still denies, --force-if-includes ALONE (a documented no-op without --force-with-lease) denies, and a --dry-run push carrying any force or delete spelling is judged like the real thing and denies. On a shell parse error, OR when a command-word wrapper hides git so no parsed segment resolves to git, it falls back to a conservative raw scan that ASKS (never a hard deny, never a silent allow) on an apparent git force-push (any -f/--force/--for-prefix/--mirror/--all form, or a +refspec anchored to start, whitespace, or either quote character, so a quoted "+main:main" under sudo is caught), an apparent branch deletion (a --de-prefix long flag, or a d carried ANYWHERE in a short - cluster, mirroring the force cluster shape so a wrapped -dv is caught, name-independent like the force spellings; or an empty-source :<protected-name> refspec, judged by its visible name), or an apparent git commit. The raw scan OVER-MATCHES by design (a case-different name, an attached -o value ending in f, an unrelated + or -d token, or prose mentioning the keywords ASKS), so re-issue a wrongly-flagged command as a plain, parseable git command. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental case, not an adversary determined to evade it.

Registry-scoped: inert with no registry or no declared mode record. Blocks a blocking question ONLY when the declared operating-mode record contains 'unattended'; attended modes, an absent mode line, and an unreadable mode record all fail OPEN (this guards one known mistake shape, a blocking prompt idling an unattended run; it is not a security boundary), with the fail-open logged to guard-events. The deny instruction distinguishes record-and-continue for ordinary decisions from record-and-HOLD for anything at the human-oversight threshold; the hook redirects the question and never licenses acting without the answer. Each denied ask appends ONE idempotent machine row keyed on session_id plus tool_use_id, carrying a bounded redacted summary (question count, length, digest), never the question text. Its behaviour is verified by the behaviour self-test. It cannot see a blocking prompt raised outside the AskUserQuestion tool.

A RECORDING substrate, not an enforcement point: it appends launch rows (a Bash call with run_in_background true, or a registry-declared dispatch tool) and completion rows (a TaskOutput read) to the machine-written dispatch ledger the stop guard consumes as its Gap-B oracle. It never blocks; a failed ledger write is surfaced as a non-blocking systemMessage, never swallowed. Coverage is exactly the hooked tools: a launch through an unhooked tool is invisible (costing one spurious stop-guard deny), a completion that never passes through TaskOutput is invisible until the staleness horizon expires the row, and the task-id extraction from tool responses is best-effort field matching. Both blind-spot directions are bounded by staleness plus the resume audit, and disclosed at the stop guard.

gates.residue: Total over the surface it examines: an OPEN merge_pending row carrying a TYPED ref (pr:N, decision:X) whose merge or record evidence exists in the declared truth sources always fails the gate. It reads only typed structured refs; a narrative number in prose, an untyped row, or a register kept outside the declared surface is out of scope by design (D9), and drift the truth sources themselves cannot see (an unpushed local merge, a PR merged under a subject with no (#N) marker) passes. In a checkout with no orchestration registry the live leg is NOT APPLICABLE (the record is machine-local by design) and the self-test carries the assurance; that scope boundary is printed, never silent.

Partial over a best-effort, adopter-configured surface. It proves preservation only for column-zero H2 headings that the adopter's own regular expressions select and that are newly introduced on the branch (present at the branch tip, absent at the unique merge-base); it catches a clean section-drop but MISSES a section that was reworded, renamed, or moved (a changed heading reads as a new-and-dropped pair, not a preserved one), never compares section bodies, does not cover edits to a heading already present at merge-base, and cannot tell a valid supersession from an opt-out marker an author simply added. Any record path or heading outside the config, and any grammar the pattern does not match, is outside its surface. The config is trusted adopter input to this preservation check: rewriting it so its heading-pattern selects fewer or no headings (semantic narrowing that makes real sections stop matching) is a change to that trusted config, not a dropped section, and defending the config against adversarial narrowing is out of this gate's threat model (it is the config-integrity surface's concern). Missing or ambiguous inputs inside the declared surface (a duplicate selected heading, an unreadable declared record, an unresolvable ref, a config path whose final or any parent component is a symlink, a non-unique merge-base on EITHER the default or the explicit-base path, an explicit --base-ref that is not that unique merge-base, an explicit --branch-ref that disagrees with the observable second parent of a two-parent post-merge commit, a default config the merge itself deleted, an uninferable branch tip) fail closed (exit 2); an explicit --base-ref is accepted only when the merge-base is unique and the ref names it, so it cannot mask a drop by naming one of several merge-bases that disagree on a section, and when the post-merge commit has two parents an explicit --branch-ref must name the observable second parent, so it cannot mask a drop by comparing against the first parent. It also strips the ambient GIT_ environment before every git call so a redirected GIT_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE cannot swap in a decoy repository, and it does not follow a symlinked config at the final or any parent component. Only with no adopter config present (a genuinely absent, not-a-symlink default) AND none at the pre-merge target is the gate NOT APPLICABLE by design; a config the merge removed, or one whose removal cannot be evaluated because the post-merge ref is unresolvable, fails closed instead. Pack CI exercises only the synthetic self-test while the adopter owns the live post-merge invocation.

hooks.residue: SessionStart cannot block at the platform (exit 2 shows stderr only, doc-confirmed 2026-08-29), so this layer SURFACES divergence and ARMS the PreToolUse resume barrier; the barrier is the mechanism. Probes, all fail-closed to a finding rather than a silent pass: the declared handoff's Branch line against the real HEAD (scrubbed read-only probe), a handoff gate marker's commit against the real HEAD commit, lease staleness, every declared record surface readable (a declared-but-unreadable surface is a cannot-evaluate FINDING, never nothing-to-check), and merge-pending rows against first-parent merge evidence. Registry-scoped; with no registry it is silent. It reads records and git state only; it cannot detect a handoff that is stale in ways its declared grammar does not carry (free-text drift), and lease MISMATCH detection is bounded to staleness because a session cannot prove its own identity against the holder field.

The mutation barrier behind orch-resume-audit, shipped WARN-FIRST (stage bake, a recorded posture): while the barrier state is armed it surfaces a systemMessage on the first mutation outside the allowlist (the record surfaces, the registry files, and the suite's own state directory stay writable, so the only exit, correcting the record, is never blocked), and it blocks nothing during the bake. The flip to deny is a manifest edit (stage to enforce, default to ask/deny) taken on recorded guard-events evidence after the bake period, per the guardrail-config-integrity discipline. Bash targets are not path-judged (a command's write targets are not lexically resolvable), so Bash mutations pass with the same surfacing only. Clearing the barrier requires re-running the audit (tools/orch_doctor.py --resume-audit) against corrected records; acknowledgement alone does not clear it.

gates.residue: Total over the declared register: a broken digest chain or sequence, a reused id, an illegal status transition, a rewrite of anchored or merge-base rows, and an unverifiable landed row always fail; a declared-but-unreadable register is exit 2. A same-authority local file offers no protection against an actor who rewrites the WHOLE chain and the anchor together, which defeats the untracked mode (the tracked mode is bounded by merge-base history instead), so rewrites are DETECTABLE within those bounds, never prevented; adopters needing real separation bind the same interface to a server-side append store. The landed-row check proves the cited commit and check path exist, not that the check semantically guards the mistake. In a checkout with no registry the live leg is NOT APPLICABLE with the self-test as assurance.

A deterministic scan over a RECOGNIZABLE SUBSET of the repo's Python launcher configuration: the generated plugin hooks.json, tools/run_all_checks.sh, every regular *.yml/*.yaml under .github/workflows/, and the optional .claude/settings.json files. A direct python3 launcher there is FAILed unless it runs isolated (-I, or the full -P -E -s), so a tool-written sibling cannot shadow a stdlib import and neuter the control; the gate itself refuses to run non-isolated (exit 2) so a sibling cannot neuter the gate first, and it fails closed (exit 2) on a missing, unreadable, non-regular, or malformed input rather than passing it as clean. It does NOT catch: wrapper or indirect launchers (a bash -c string, a .sh re-launcher), $PYTHON or shell aliases and functions, a dynamically assembled argv, the programmatic subprocess children in the tools and the regenerate strings in .aiqt/gensrc.json (a separate follow-up), a script that mutates its own sys.path at runtime (which -I cannot prevent), an unrecognized interpreter name, launcher configuration outside the enumerated surfaces, YAML or shell constructs beyond the supported line grammar, and the PATH provenance of python3 itself; a python3 token embedded in a quoted argument or a heredoc may be miscounted.

A pattern scanner for hardcoded credentials: it catches recognizable provider-token prefixes (now including Google, Stripe, GitLab, SendGrid, npm, PyPI upload, and Slack webhook shapes), assignments of a literal to a credential-named variable, and (GD-121) high-entropy literals of 40 or more characters assigned to a generic credential-like name (Shannon entropy at least 3.5 bits per character judged on the token's first 150 characters, letters and digits required, placeholders and environment lookups excluded, metadata-named variables excluded). It still misses a keyword-free high-entropy string (the opaque-name class, R1, the measured residue of 2026-08-08 shared with gitleaks), a generic-keyword value of 12 to 39 characters that gitleaks can flag below the local 40-character floor (R3, a deliberate noise-control choice, confirmed against pinned gitleaks 8.30.1), a real secret held under a metadata-named variable such as public_key or key_path (excluded by design in the safe direction, where CI still catches it, R4); a deferred provider family (a Twilio-class short-prefix-over-hex or a Telegram bot token, left to gitleaks, R2); a secret split across lines or assembled by concatenation, an encoded secret, or a secret in a binary (R5); and an unquoted value that begins with an environment-lookup root such as process.env., treated as a reference not a literal (R6). Detection here is a compensating control, never a substitute for keeping the secret out of the repository in the first place.

hooks.residue: A COMPENSATING control, not a replacement: the CI secret-scan and gitleaks gates remain the broader backstop, and this layer moves the same high-signal detection to the moment a secret would be written, so an accidental paste is caught before it lands on disk rather than only at commit or CI time. It SINGLE-SOURCES its shapes from tools/check_secrets.py (the pack source of truth), rendered into the handler by tools/gen_secret_patterns.py and drift-gated so the two can never fork: the recognizable provider-token PREFIX shapes (GitHub, GitHub fine-grained PAT, OpenAI-style, OpenAI project key, Anthropic, AWS access key id, Slack, Slack app-level token, a private key block header, a JWT, and (GD-121) Google API key, Stripe live and test, GitLab personal access token, SendGrid, npm, PyPI upload token, and a Slack incoming-webhook URL), the credential-named ASSIGN shape (a passwd/password/secret/token/api-key/access-key/client-secret/auth-token/private-key/credential variable assigned a literal of real length), and (GD-121) an ENTROPY-GATED generic-assignment shape: a token of 40 or more characters (Shannon entropy at least 3.5 bits per character judged on its first 150 characters, letters and digits required) assigned to a generic credential-like name matched on EXACT components (key/auth/token/secret/passphrase/creds/... so apiKey and client-secret match while monkey and author do not), with placeholders and environment lookups excluded before the entropy test and a metadata-named left-hand side (id/name/version/url/path/public/...) excluded. It EXCLUDES obvious placeholders (the shared PLACEHOLDER shape: your/my/the-prefixed names, change-me, example, sample, dummy, redacted, fake, test, todo, none, null, n/a, an angle-bracket or dollar-brace or dollar-VAR template, and runs of x/dot/star), and for an UNQUOTED assignment value it additionally requires both a letter and a digit, exactly as check_secrets.py does, so ordinary prose does not trip it. It scans the content a Write would write, the new_string an Edit would introduce, the concatenation of the new_string values a MultiEdit would introduce across its edits, or the command string a Bash call would emit, and DENIES on a real match, naming only the pattern label and never echoing the secret value. DISCLOSED non-catches: a KEYWORD-FREE high-entropy value (an opaque = <hex> with no credential keyword near it): both this scanner and gitleaks miss it (R1, the measured residue of 2026-08-08); a generic-keyword value of 12 to 39 characters, below the local 40-character floor, which gitleaks can still flag (R3, a deliberate noise-control choice confirmed against pinned gitleaks 8.30.1); a real secret held under a metadata-named variable such as public_key or key_path, excluded here in the safe direction where the CI scan still catches it (R4); a secret written by a tool other than Write, Edit, MultiEdit, or Bash (other content tools such as NotebookEdit are out of scope, routed to a periodic pattern review); a secret split across tokens or lines or assembled by concatenation, since the scan is per-line and lexical; on the Bash path the command string is scanned as RAW TEXT (it is not shlex-tokenized and is not executed), so a secret assembled by concatenation or supplied through a shell variable or expansion is missed, but a redirect or an embedded # does NOT cause a Bash-path miss; the ASSIGN shape also does not match a JSON-style quoted credential key ("api_key": "...") or a triple-quoted value, a curated-pattern-set format-completeness gap routed to the periodic pattern review (backlog L12); a deferred provider family (a Twilio-class short-prefix-over-hex or a Telegram bot token, left to gitleaks, R2); an unquoted value beginning with an environment-lookup root such as process.env., treated as a reference not a literal (R6); and a base64-encoded or otherwise obfuscated form. gitleaks in CI is a BROADER independent scanner and a stronger net, but it is NOT exhaustive (it too misses the keyword-free entropy class R1), so it is a compensating layer, never a guarantee. It is BEST-EFFORT: it targets the accidental paste or commit, not an adversary deliberately encoding or fragmenting a secret to evade it.

A BEST-EFFORT QUOTE-AWARE LEXICAL check via the shared tokenizer (_lex_command); it is ASK-only, so a detected substitution is surfaced for confirmation rather than blocked, and it makes NO soundness or universal-coverage claim. In a parsed simple segment it resolves the effective command word past leading shell assignments and the recognized command modifiers command, exec, builtin, nohup, time, !, and env; for env it skips leading option tokens, the separated operands of common value-taking options, and NAME=VALUE assignments. When that word is literal git and the subcommand after recognized Git-global options is literal commit, it scans EVERY argv token after commit, including tokens after `--` or `--end-of-options`, for a backtick or $( marker in a substituting double-quoted or unquoted context, using the shared lexer's parallel per-token opacity plus the narrow unquoted-$( split form where a final opaque token ending in $ is immediately followed by the ( operator. It deliberately does no Git option binding because the shell expands argv before Git parses it. On an unparseable command, the raw fallback ASKS when coarse git-commit and substitution-marker probes both match; that fallback can over-match quoted prose or literal markers. HONEST RESIDUALS: the option tokens belonging to a recognized command modifier are not skipped (for example command -p git commit, time -p git commit, exec -c git commit, exec -a x git commit, and nohup -- git commit), so resolution advances one word past the modifier, stops on the option, and silently ALLOWs a substitution-bearing commit; command modifiers outside the recognized set (notably sudo, nice, timeout, doas, stdbuf, and ionice) are not resolved, so for example sudo git commit -m "$(x)" silently ALLOWs; reserved-word compounds (if/while/until and `{ ...; }`) are not parsed through to their inner git command; shell functions and aliases that rename git; git-config subcommand aliases (for example alias.ci=commit making git ci -m "$(x)") cannot be known lexically and silently ALLOW; sh -c or bash -c script bodies; eval or xargs indirection; redirect targets on a recognized commit segment are removed from argv by the lexer and are not scanned, so git commit -m ok > "$(x)" and git commit -m ok 2> "`x`" silently ALLOW; leading environment-assignment values and Git-global option/value tokens before commit; a pre-subcommand unquoted $( that fragments the lexer segment, letting the whole commit invocation including its message escape inspection; quote-mangled command words such as g''it are outside the claimed command-resolution surface even where the shared lexer happens to normalize a form to git; $VAR indirection, concatenation, PATH-shadowed commands, and any other non-literal command word that does not resolve lexically to git; commands outside the Bash tool; and unparseable commands beyond the raw fallback probes. Deliberate over-ASKs: $((...)) includes $(; a bare $ immediately before an escaped parenthesis (for example git commit -m $\(x\)) is marked opaque and the decoded-marker check sees $(, so it ASKS even though Bash passes literal $(x) and runs no substitution; ANSI-C $'...' is treated as an opaque marker-bearing token even though Bash does not substitute inside it; whole-token opacity means an escaped literal backtick or $( sharing a word with an unrelated unquoted expansion or glob prompts; and a post-boundary pathspec produced by substitution (for example git commit -- $(ls)) prompts because the shell still executes it. It targets the accidental case, not an adversary.

A PATH guard, not a content judge: it decides where a write lands, never what it writes. Covers only PreToolUse Write, Edit, and MultiEdit calls carrying a readable file_path. TWO arming inputs, each fail-open on genuine ABSENCE only: the per-slice declaration write-scope.json, read at the orchestration registry-declared state_dir (resolved from the registry the guard reads EXACTLY ONCE, via the pure _state_dir_from_registry helper, never a second independently-faulting read; out of the slice tree by default but MAY be in-tree when the registry declares an in-tree state_dir), arms SLICE CONFINEMENT; the in-tree committed frozen floor .aiqt/frozen.json (generated by tools/gen_manifest.py from the ownership classification, drift-gated) arms the FROZEN layer. The structural other-repo/nested-repo denial applies to every covered write whose repository root resolves; the frozen-floor denial fires whenever a floor is PRESENT, and an armed session additionally requires one, so neither is unconditionally always-on and only an un-armed session with a genuinely-absent floor leaves the frozen layer inert. Slice confinement is fail-open on a missing declaration. The principled fail-open is genuine ABSENCE (of a declaration or floor: no confinement in effect, the same inert boundary gensrc and the orchestration suite use); a cannot-evaluate FAULT is not absence and denies (see the fail posture below). The registry that LOCATES the declaration is part of the read: a bad or unreadable registry (an lstat fault, a read/parse error, a non-version-1 object, or a present-but-malformed state_dir) is a cannot-evaluate that DENIES rather than silently falling back to XDG and disarming confinement. Out-of-scope is a DENY, never an ASK (an ASK would hand the confined actor the click-through on its own confinement and would wedge an unattended run); the remedy is the harness re-declaring the slice, so scope-widening stays on the harness side, never a guarded-tool call. The declaration is machine-set inert data, never authored by the assistant through a guarded tool; the residual Bash-write path to the state dir remains, so the harness-set integrity is defence in depth, not categorical. Fail posture, by regime: a MISSING tool_name denies (the shared fail-closed contract); a malformed tool_name, an unreadable tool_input, a missing/empty file_path, or a control-character file_path denies as a malformed call in either regime; a covered write whose session repository root cannot be resolved (a missing/unreadable cwd or a non-git session) DENIES fail-closed in both regimes, because the root is resolved FIRST and containment cannot be evaluated without it, so this denial precedes any relative-path handling (a non-git relative-path write DENIES, it does not defer); only WHEN the root resolves does an un-armed relative file_path defer to the sibling absolute_paths hook (which owns the relative case, EN-8 making no cwd-trusting determination) and allow, while an armed relative file_path denies; an un-armed realpath/containment/nested-repo-probe FAULT now DENIES too (a cannot-evaluate: the guard cannot prove the target is in-repo and not nested, so it denies rather than allowing an unverified write), as the same fault does armed; a target proven OUTSIDE the session toplevel, or in a NESTED or FOREIGN git repository under or beside it (resolved via the scrubbed git toplevel of the target nearest existing ancestor, every ambient GIT_* removed so a decoy repo cannot redirect the read), denies in BOTH regimes; a present frozen floor with the target on it denies in both regimes (the floor outranks the allowlist, deny over allow), a present-but-malformed floor denies (cannot-evaluate), and an ABSENT floor is inert un-armed but denies while armed (an armed session must commit a floor, an explicit empty list being valid, so a Bash-deleted floor cannot silently downgrade an armed session); armed, a declaration that is unreadable, malformed, unknown-version, or whose worktree_root does not resolve to this repo (a stale, copied, or moved declaration) denies; an allow entry wholly on the frozen floor makes the declaration malformed and denies (a declaration cannot declare past the floor); a target in repo, not frozen, and in the declared slice scope allows silently, while one not in scope denies. Every deny attempts a BEST-EFFORT guard-events append (the over-fire metric) where the root is resolvable: the append can fail silently (_orch_append_jsonl returns False and the deny ignores it), which neither blocks nor alters the denial and may lose the over-fire metric for that event. Matching is on canonicalized real paths with component-boundary tree containment (the gensrc idiom), never a raw string prefix; the declaration and floor share one entry grammar (a repo-root-relative POSIX path, a trailing / marks a tree, no absolute/backslash/./../control-char/wildcard component). The floor is enforced against the manifest CLASS set {derived, manifest-self, archive}. The RUNTIME value of that floor is un-lowerable by the constrained actor through the guarded tools (a guarded write to .aiqt/frozen.json is itself on the floor and denied); but its DEFINITION (FROZEN_CLASSES in tools/gen_manifest.py) is generator source that lands through pull-request review PLUS the drift gate, which detects an INCONSISTENT floor (a committed frozen.json that does not match a fresh regeneration), NOT an unauthorized-but-internally-consistent redefinition of the class set followed by regeneration; an independent floor-authorization mechanism is out of scope for this hook. The floor proves membership in its declared selector set only, not that the generation-time class mapping is semantically complete. Class c (partial), matching the sibling gensrc_guard: the control fires deterministically inside its Write|Edit|MultiEdit matcher, but the rules it enforces span write paths the matcher cannot see (Bash-mediated writes, NotebookEdit, filesystem MCP tools, any write outside the platform hook path), and its slice-arming state is machine-local, so CI cannot observe the confinement. The committed frozen floor .aiqt/frozen.json is a generated, drift-gated output backstopped at merge by the manifest-gen-drift gate (tools/gen_manifest.py --check), the gensrc-registry-drift gate (tools/gen_gensrc.py --check), and the independent manifest-integrity verifier (tools/check_manifest.py) (defence in depth, each catching the other residual; these CI gates are not removed or softened), but nothing backstops an uncommitted, out-of-scope-mutable, or cross-repository write through the uncovered channels. Realpath closes symlink escapes present at check time but not a post-check swap, hard-link alias, bind-mount change, or case-fold/Unicode alias between the lstat probe and the tool write (TOCTOU); an OS-level write sandbox is the stronger overlapping control where available. It is single-author by design: exactly one declaration, one writer, harness-replaced; it is confinement of the sole writer, not parallel-write collision arbitration.

SessionStart cannot block at the platform (exit 2 shows stderr only, doc-confirmed 2026-08-29), so this layer SURFACES divergence and ARMS the PreToolUse resume barrier; the barrier is the mechanism. Probes, all fail-closed to a finding rather than a silent pass: the declared handoff's Branch line against the real HEAD (scrubbed read-only probe), a handoff gate marker's commit against the real HEAD commit, lease staleness, every declared record surface readable (a declared-but-unreadable surface is a cannot-evaluate FINDING, never nothing-to-check), and merge-pending rows against first-parent merge evidence. Registry-scoped; with no registry it is silent. It reads records and git state only; it cannot detect a handoff that is stale in ways its declared grammar does not carry (free-text drift), and lease MISMATCH detection is bounded to staleness because a session cannot prove its own identity against the holder field.

The mutation barrier behind orch-resume-audit, shipped WARN-FIRST (stage bake, a recorded posture): while the barrier state is armed it surfaces a systemMessage on the first mutation outside the allowlist (the record surfaces, the registry files, and the suite's own state directory stay writable, so the only exit, correcting the record, is never blocked), and it blocks nothing during the bake. The flip to deny is a manifest edit (stage to enforce, default to ask/deny) taken on recorded guard-events evidence after the bake period, per the guardrail-config-integrity discipline. Bash targets are not path-judged (a command's write targets are not lexically resolvable), so Bash mutations pass with the same surfacing only. Clearing the barrier requires re-running the audit (tools/orch_doctor.py --resume-audit) against corrected records; acknowledgement alone does not clear it.

REGISTRY-SCOPED: entirely inert unless an orchestration registry (.aiqt/orchestration.local.json or .aiqt/orchestration.json) is present AND a declared orchestrator lease or mode record is live, so plain Q&A sessions and bounded workers never inherit the global backlog. FAIL-OPEN on its own I/O errors, none of which wedges the session: an unresolvable cwd or an inactive-or-unreadable lease/mode scope SILENTLY ALLOWS the stop (no warn banner, no guard-event); an unreadable registry ALLOWS with a warn banner but no guard-event; and an unreadable turn-state takes the bounded loop-bound exit. But (FIX 1) an enumerator error or timeout, and any cannot-evaluate (an unreadable proof source), FAIL CLOSED-CONTINUE: the stop is DENIED (ignorance refuses the wind-down), releasable by the operator-owned escape sentinel and never a clean close, bounded by the guard-owned loop bound past which it becomes a deliberate, recorded forced exit. The deny is BOUNDED: the guard's own persisted counter (turn-state, reset on genuine human input) allows at most two denies per epoch, then ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS, independent of any platform loop field (none is documented on Stop; a loop-ish payload field is honoured opportunistically if one ever appears). The operator escape sentinel yields the clean ALLOW only when it passes enforced acceptance: a regular file (never a symlink), owned by a uid other than the guard's effective uid, and not group- or other-writable; a present sentinel failing any condition is IGNORED with the decision unchanged, recorded to guard-events and escape-spoof.json, and surfaced once by the next resume audit. Uid inequality proves not-self, never operator identity; on a shared-uid host no file either party can create passes, so the clean-ALLOW channel is unavailable there (recovery: a differently-owned sentinel such as a root-owned one, operator registry or mode maintenance, or the bounded marked exit; split-uid deployment is the recommended posture). The platform interrupt is a second, structurally unguardable escape, left uncovered on purpose. Blocker proofs are validated against their declared sources (the dispatch ledger, the pending-decisions surface, evidence freshness, the clock), but that whole substantiation surface (the backlog state/granted fields, a pending-decision row, the dispatch ledger, a not-before value, and free-text external evidence) is largely ACTOR-AUTHORABLE: the guard raises the bar (it rejects an unknown blocker kind and requires a substantiating record in the declared authoritative source) yet cannot categorically enforce that a block is granted by an authority other than the assistant, closed categorically only by operator-owned, assistant-non-writable records at the OS layer (SYSTEM-HARDENING.md entry 2). Plausibly FABRICATED external evidence in particular is not mechanically closable at this layer where no attestation register is declared; where one is declared, an external or foreign-lease blocker classifies blocked only when its ref is covered by a fresh validated attestation whose snapshot is re-anchored to the register authority and whose refs are re-derived from the register content at yield, so a swapped register or a fabricated-refs snapshot substantiates nothing; this raises the bar over free-text evidence but is not categorically forgery-proof, since the register is a separately-declared surface and filesystem write to it, wherever it is declared, forges an attestation by appending a valid approved row (uncommitted; the git or anchor authority checks only the committed or anchored prefix), closed categorically only by an operator-owned, assistant-non-writable register at the OS layer; the remaining residuals are cadence, since tamper misleads until the next audit or gate run, and relevance, since a resolving pointer can still be a misappropriated pretext that triage refutes). The human-decision class proves only that a pending-decision row exists, never that the item genuinely crosses the human-oversight threshold, which stays human judgement. Coverage is the rendered roster (Stop, TeammateIdle, the yield-tool matcher): a yield primitive outside that roster is uncovered, reconciled when the toolchain register changes. The dispatch ledger sees only hooked launch tools, so a task launched through an unhooked tool costs one spurious deny and a dead task read as live permits one idle until staleness catches it, both directions bounded and logged. An open or proposed id that vanishes from the enumeration without a closed receipt, OR (FIX 2) a previously-actionable id DEMOTED to proposed/ungranted without a closed receipt (the checkpoint records each id's eligibility for this), is injected as a cannot-evaluate by the anti-shrinkage checkpoint (backlog-checkpoint.json: the first window has no union to compare, and a drop forced by the checkpoint's id bound is logged, never silent); that eligibility memory is itself in the actor-writable state dir, the same categorical residual. A bound-released ALLOW WITH FINDINGS past ANY non-closed disposition (actionable, cannot-evaluate, waiting, blocked, or proposed) is marked forced_unresolved (a guard-events row plus an append-only row in forced-exit.jsonl, each surfaced exactly once via forced-exit-surfaced.json, a failed record surfacing in the warn banner itself) and is triaged by the next resume audit; no register row, attestation, or escape-adjacent artefact suppresses that record.

The TeammateIdle binding of the same decision core as orch-stop-guard, sharing its registry/lease scoping, escape, counter bound, and guard-events logging. A deny (exit 2) prevents the teammate from going idle past enumerated actionable work. On cannot-evaluate (an enumerator error or an unreadable proof source) it takes the STOP branch, which (FIX 1) now DENIES the idle (ignorance refuses the wind-down; a denied TeammateIdle cannot wedge the session, and the operator escape releases a genuine block); an unreadable registry or unresolvable cwd still fails OPEN at the binding. Same disclosed bounds as orch-stop-guard on ledger blind spots, fabricated blocker evidence and its attestation narrowing, escape-sentinel acceptance, the anti-shrinkage checkpoint, and the forced_unresolved marking of bound-released exits. Fires only where the platform emits TeammateIdle (doc-confirmed 2026-08-29); platforms without the event keep only the Stop and yield-tool bindings.

The scheduled-yield binding of the decision core: a call that parks the run (schedule_idle) or ends the loop (a ScheduleWakeup with stop=true is classified stop) is judged against a fresh enumeration. Registry-scoped and lease-scoped like orch-stop-guard; a tool the registry's yield_tools list does not name is out of scope even inside the matcher, and a registry yield tool OUTSIDE this fixed matcher is NOT covered (the doctor flags it; a manifest matcher is fixed at generation). On the schedule path a cannot-evaluate DENIES (missing evidence never licenses new autonomy; a denied tool call cannot wedge a session), bounded by a three-denial cap on an unchanged basis, after which it ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS so the guard cannot be farmed into bypass training. That cap needs persistable, readable turn-state; when the state directory is unreadable or unwritable the denial count cannot accumulate, so the schedule path stays fail-closed to DENY (the safe direction: the run keeps working rather than idling) and the cap does not relieve. Wake hygiene: a permitted schedule must name the tracked item or blocker it will recheck in its own text, judged by token containment (a paraphrase that names neither id nor ref denies once, a disclosed over-fire). The quiet-duration check is a best-effort regex: it fires only when the call text carries a parseable minutes claim AND turn-state carries a measured gap, and then the measured figure wins; an unparseable claim or an unknown measured endpoint authorizes nothing and is not invented. A fired timer or an existing cron is never counted as a live task or a blocker. Escape-sentinel acceptance, the attestation narrowing of external and foreign-lease evidence, and the anti-shrinkage checkpoint are shared with orch-stop-guard; cap or bound relief past any non-closed disposition (actionable, cannot-evaluate, waiting, blocked, or proposed) is marked forced_unresolved (a guard-events row plus an append-only row in forced-exit.jsonl, surfaced once via forced-exit-surfaced.json), a failed record surfacing in the returned systemMessage.

A RECORDING substrate, not an enforcement point: it appends launch rows (a Bash call with run_in_background true, or a registry-declared dispatch tool) and completion rows (a TaskOutput read) to the machine-written dispatch ledger the stop guard consumes as its Gap-B oracle. It never blocks; a failed ledger write is surfaced as a non-blocking systemMessage, never swallowed. Coverage is exactly the hooked tools: a launch through an unhooked tool is invisible (costing one spurious stop-guard deny), a completion that never passes through TaskOutput is invisible until the staleness horizon expires the row, and the task-id extraction from tool responses is best-effort field matching. Both blind-spot directions are bounded by staleness plus the resume audit, and disclosed at the stop guard.

An open or proposed id that vanishes from the enumeration without a closed receipt, OR (FIX 2) a previously-actionable id DEMOTED to proposed/ungranted without a closed receipt (the checkpoint records each id's eligibility for this), is injected as a cannot-evaluate by the anti-shrinkage checkpoint (backlog-checkpoint.json: the first window has no union to compare, and a drop forced by the checkpoint's id bound is logged, never silent); that eligibility memory is itself in the actor-writable state dir, the same categorical residual. A bound-released ALLOW WITH FINDINGS past ANY non-closed disposition (actionable, cannot-evaluate, waiting, blocked, or proposed) is marked forced_unresolved (a guard-events row plus an append-only row in forced-exit.jsonl, each surfaced exactly once via forced-exit-surfaced.json, a failed record surfacing in the warn banner itself) and is triaged by the next resume audit; no register row, attestation, or escape-adjacent artefact suppresses that record.

The TeammateIdle binding of the same decision core as orch-stop-guard, sharing its registry/lease scoping, escape, counter bound, and guard-events logging. A deny (exit 2) prevents the teammate from going idle past enumerated actionable work. On cannot-evaluate (an enumerator error or an unreadable proof source) it takes the STOP branch, which (FIX 1) now DENIES the idle (ignorance refuses the wind-down; a denied TeammateIdle cannot wedge the session, and the operator escape releases a genuine block); an unreadable registry or unresolvable cwd still fails OPEN at the binding. Same disclosed bounds as orch-stop-guard on ledger blind spots, fabricated blocker evidence and its attestation narrowing, escape-sentinel acceptance, the anti-shrinkage checkpoint, and the forced_unresolved marking of bound-released exits. Fires only where the platform emits TeammateIdle (doc-confirmed 2026-08-29); platforms without the event keep only the Stop and yield-tool bindings.

AIRTIGHT-NARROW (round 32, maintainer-directed simplification): this guard does NO shell parsing, so no lexical, quoting, or operator edge can make it credit a capture that does not exist. It governs a background dispatch (run_in_background is true) with the capture-proof test below, and adds ONE narrow foreground branch (L-GS1): a foreground call (run_in_background not true) is out of scope EXCEPT that a bare '&' control operator, which detaches a child into asynchronous work this tool call does not track, is an ASK steering the operator to the tracked background dispatch. That foreground detector is a dedicated quote- and escape-tracking scan (not the shared segmenter, which strips quote and escape provenance and would misread a quoted or escaped ampersand as a separator): it distinguishes the detach '&' from the shell forms that also carry an ampersand but do not detach ('&&', '&>', '&>>', '<&', '>&', '|&', and any single-quoted, double-quoted, or backslash-escaped ampersand, and an '&' inside an unquoted word-start '#' comment, which is dropped). It catches ONLY a bare '&' operator in the OUTER command string, and a scan that ends still inside an unbalanced quote, or inside an ANSI-C dollar-single-quote construct ($'...') this scan does not model, could hide a real trailing '&', so it FAILS TOWARD THE ASK rather than silently allowing. HONEST RESIDUAL (disclose-guard-residuals): detachment achieved WITHOUT a bare '&' in the outer command is NOT caught and is SILENTLY ALLOWED, not over-asked - a runtime detacher that backgrounds with no '&' (setsid, disown, coproc; nohup is normally written with a trailing '&', which IS caught), a nested shell string whose '&' sits inside quotes (bash -c '... &'), and an alias or function that renames a detacher; the grammar cases that OVER-ask instead are NOT a single case: any unquoted '&' this scan does not model as a detach still reaches the scan and reads as an operator, so it asks when no detach is present. Examples are a here-document body carrying a literal '&', and an arithmetic expansion such as $(( a & b )) where '&' is bitwise-AND; any other construct this scan does not model that leaves a non-detach '&' unquoted in the outer string over-asks the same way. The guard roots via the scrubbed rev-parse primitive (git rev-parse --show-toplevel with every ambient GIT_* removed), so it does use git for session rooting; the AIRTIGHT-NARROW claim is about the command-string analysis doing NO shell parsing, not about avoiding git.Approving that ASK does not itself create tracking; only converting to run_in_background=true lets the dispatch ledger record the launch. The foreground branch stays registry-scoped, so a non-orchestrated session acquires no new prompt. A background dispatch is ALLOWED only when the whole command is drawn from a conservative safe character set (letters, digits, space and tab, and the punctuation '_ - . / = : @ , + %'), so it carries NO shell metacharacter (no pipe, redirect, separator, quote, expansion, command or process substitution, grouping, glob, comment, tilde, history, or newline) and is not a shell reserved word (coproc, which backgrounds a coprocess whose output the harness does not capture, or a compound/prefix keyword such as if/for/while/time) and its full stdout reaches the harness capture that run_in_background binds to the TaskOutput completion signal IN THE COMMON CASE - unless the invoked program or wrapper itself detaches, daemonizes, or redirects that output, which is out of view (see the program-behaviour residual below). ANY other command is an ASK: the guard does not parse shell syntax to prove or disprove capture, so it asks the operator to confirm the full output lands in a durable capture (redirect the producer's own stdout to a real file, or make a real-file tee the final stage). DISCLOSED COVERAGE BOUND (deliberate, not a defect): this trades COVERAGE for a guarantee of NO SHELL-SYNTAX FALSE-ALLOW (no quoting or parsing edge in the dispatch string can fabricate a capture). A legitimate captured background dispatch that uses any shell syntax (a real-file redirect, a tee, a glob, an env-assignment prefix carrying a quote) is ASKED rather than proven, and the guard never actively DENIES a parsed command; the operator's confirmation at the ASK, and the vrfdlv delivery-marker discipline, are the compensating layers. What this buys over a lexical capture-proof: the ALLOW rests on a raw-character test that no quoting or parsing can fool, so there is no shell-syntax edge that can silently open a false allow. The residual is RUNTIME behaviour beyond the dispatch string: a plain command can still fail to deliver its full output to durable capture for reasons no pre-execution command-string check can show. Two classes. (a) The invoked program or wrapper's own behaviour - a terminal multiplexer or setsid that detaches, a start-stop-daemon or nohup-style wrapper that backgrounds or redirects the producer's stdout (e.g. --output /dev/null), a program that internally pipes to head/tail, or one that sources a script or resolves a PATH name to a truncating tool. (b) Platform and resource limits - the harness's own TaskOutput capture has a size ceiling (Claude Code terminates a background task whose output exceeds a documented limit), so a very large stream is lost at the harness regardless of the command, and disk-full, a kill signal, or other run-time conditions can likewise cut delivery short. None of this appears in the command string. The guard's ALLOW therefore asserts only that no shell SYNTAX in the dispatch string can defeat capture; whether the output actually and fully reaches durable capture is a run-time property that the post-execution vrfdlv delivery-marker discipline, not this guard, confirms. The only DENY is the fail-closed case of a background dispatch carrying no readable command string.

Registry-scoped deny companion to orch-truncation-guard's bare-& ASK (defence in depth on the same PreToolUse Bash event): inert with no orchestration registry present, and NOT lease-scoped (a bounded worker building a fire-and-forget poll is equally wrong). It DENIES only an UNAMBIGUOUS canonical shape recognized by a best-effort LEXICAL heuristic, a status-polling loop detached with a SINGLE bare '&' that is the command's FINAL operator: exactly ONE for/while/until loop closed by a bare-'&' 'done', whose body carries a 'sleep' command word and whose construct (the loop condition through 'done') carries a status probe. The probe test is a deliberate HEURISTIC, not an enumeration of every status tool: a 'gh' or 'curl' command word, a '--watch' token, or a token with an 'actions/runs' path component; a poll driven by another probe command is a disclosed miss, not a match. Reserved words (for/while/until/do/done) are recognized ONLY as the EXACT raw-unquoted token: because argv is quote-decoded and the command-word helper basenames, a bare '&' closing a command whose name was written quoted, or a path such as '/tmp/done', is NOT read as the loop terminator (it classifies 'none'), and an inner loop header that shares a segment with the outer 'do' is still counted from the raw-unquoted tokens rather than borrowing the outer loop's probe. The classifier is THREE-VALUED over the shared quote/redirect-aware lexer (_lex_command). It is 'none' on a full parse that is simply not the canonical shape: no bare '&'; a bare '&' that does not close a raw-unquoted 'done' terminator (for example 'sleep 30 &', a quoted or path 'done', or a 'done' carrying a redirect such as 'done >log &'); or a clean single loop lacking the sleep or the probe. It is 'indeterminate', emitting nothing and deferring to the truncation guard's generic bare-'&' ASK on the same event, whenever the structure cannot be soundly attributed to one canonical loop, so it never fabricates a deny: an unparseable construct (heredoc, here-string, process substitution, unbalanced quote, NUL, malformed redirect); any subshell or C-style '(( ))' grouping (a '(' or ')' separator); more than one bare '&'; a command trailing the bare-'&' 'done'; a nested or extra loop keyword (a second for/while/until/do or a second 'done', counted from the raw-unquoted tokens); a conditional reserved word (if/then/elif/else/fi/case/esac or a '!' negation) anywhere in the loop span; or brace grouping ('{' or '}') in the loop span. This conservative posture is deliberate for a BLOCK guard: a false 'match' would strand a session, so any ambiguity defers to the ASK rather than deny. HONEST RESIDUALS (disclose-guard-residuals): detachment with no bare '&' in the outer command (setsid, disown, coproc, an aliased or function-renamed detacher, a nested bash -c '... &'), and a poll loop hidden inside a command substitution (opaque to the segment walk), are NOT caught and are silently allowed here; a nested loop, a conditional or brace-grouped body, a C-style for '(( ))', a multi-detach command, and a subshell-grouped or unparseable detach are 'indeterminate' here and left to the truncation guard's ASK, not denied. Quoting is derived from raw character positions (argv_opaque flags an unquoted expansion/glob/brace/tilde but NOT plain quoting), so the raw-unquoted reserved-word checks read seg.raw directly. Fail-open (silent allow) on a non-Bash or absent tool, an absent registry, and a non-string or empty command; a present-but-malformed registry leaves the guard active (deny-safe direction). The 'trkasy' rule text already carries the untracked-wait-loop clause; this hook enforces it and adds no rule.

A RECORDING substrate: stamps the clock-read UTC time of each GENUINE human prompt into turn-state (resetting the stop guard's deny counters), classifies a prompt matching a registered wake as timer-originated (not stamping it), and injects a measured-gap context line so any quiet-duration reasoning uses the measured figure. It never blocks. Classification is digest matching against wake registrations this suite itself recorded: a wake fired through a mechanism the suite never saw is stamped as genuine human input (the safe direction: it only narrows guard autonomy). An unknown prior stamp yields an 'unknown' gap that authorizes nothing.

The scheduled-yield binding of the decision core: a call that parks the run (schedule_idle) or ends the loop (a ScheduleWakeup with stop=true is classified stop) is judged against a fresh enumeration. Registry-scoped and lease-scoped like orch-stop-guard; a tool the registry's yield_tools list does not name is out of scope even inside the matcher, and a registry yield tool OUTSIDE this fixed matcher is NOT covered (the doctor flags it; a manifest matcher is fixed at generation). On the schedule path a cannot-evaluate DENIES (missing evidence never licenses new autonomy; a denied tool call cannot wedge a session), bounded by a three-denial cap on an unchanged basis, after which it ALLOWS WITH FINDINGS so the guard cannot be farmed into bypass training. That cap needs persistable, readable turn-state; when the state directory is unreadable or unwritable the denial count cannot accumulate, so the schedule path stays fail-closed to DENY (the safe direction: the run keeps working rather than idling) and the cap does not relieve. Wake hygiene: a permitted schedule must name the tracked item or blocker it will recheck in its own text, judged by token containment (a paraphrase that names neither id nor ref denies once, a disclosed over-fire). The quiet-duration check is a best-effort regex: it fires only when the call text carries a parseable minutes claim AND turn-state carries a measured gap, and then the measured figure wins; an unparseable claim or an unknown measured endpoint authorizes nothing and is not invented. A fired timer or an existing cron is never counted as a live task or a blocker. Escape-sentinel acceptance, the attestation narrowing of external and foreign-lease evidence, and the anti-shrinkage checkpoint are shared with orch-stop-guard; cap or bound relief past any non-closed disposition (actionable, cannot-evaluate, waiting, blocked, or proposed) is marked forced_unresolved (a guard-events row plus an append-only row in forced-exit.jsonl, surfaced once via forced-exit-surfaced.json), a failed record surfacing in the returned systemMessage.
